units.excerpt: Our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) is our voluntary framework for managing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems. It establishes how we identify and evaluate risks, how we make decisions about AI development and deployment, and, from the perspective of the world at large, how we aim to make sure that the benefits of our models exceed their costs.
units.paraphrase: The RSP is described as a voluntary framework governing risk identification, development/deployment decisions, and ensuring model benefits exceed costs.

units.excerpt: We have always intended for our RSP to be a living document. We will continually update the RSP as we learn more about AI capabilities and risks, develop and refine technical safety measures, and gain more experience navigating an ecosystem in which the risks to society depend on the actions of many developers.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic states the RSP is intended as a living document that will be continually updated as understanding grows.

units.excerpt: The major components of this third iteration are as follows:
units.paraphrase: This sentence introduces a list of the major components of the third iteration of the RSP.

units.excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety outline what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
units.paraphrase: Industry-wide safety recommendations describe what is needed across the industry to keep catastrophic risks low during rapid AI advances.

units.excerpt: We lay this out in a table that maps capability thresholds to the mitigations we believe they call for. We also include our planned mitigations as a company, which are drawn from other sections of this policy and associated artifacts.
units.paraphrase: A table maps capability thresholds to called-for mitigations, and also lists company-specific planned mitigations drawn from elsewhere in the policy.

units.excerpt: This approach represents a change from our previous RSP, driven by a collective action problem. The overall level of catastrophic risk from AI depends on the actions of multiple AI developers, not just one.
units.paraphrase: This approach changed from the prior RSP due to a collective action problem, since overall catastrophic risk depends on multiple developers' actions.

units.excerpt: Our previous RSP committed to implementing mitigations that would reduce our models' absolute risk levels to acceptable levels, without regard to whether other frontier AI developers would do the same.
units.paraphrase: The previous RSP focused on reducing absolute risk levels regardless of other developers' actions.

units.excerpt: But from a societal perspective, what matters is the risk to the ecosystem as a whole. If one AI developer paused development to implement safety measures while others moved forward training and deploying AI systems without strong mitigations, that could result in a world that is less safe—the developers with the weakest protections would set the pace, and responsible developers would lose their ability to do safety research and advance the public benefit.
units.paraphrase: Ecosystem-wide risk matters more than individual risk, since a developer pausing unilaterally could let weaker developers set the pace, reducing overall safety.

units.excerpt: Although this situation has not yet arisen, it looks likely enough that we want to prepare for it.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic states it wants to prepare for this scenario even though it has not yet occurred.

units.excerpt: We now separate our plans as a company—those which we expect to achieve regardless of what any other company does—from our more ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic distinguishes its own unilateral company plans from its more ambitious industry-wide recommendations.

units.excerpt: We aspire to advance the latter through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy. But we cannot commit to following them unilaterally.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic aims to advance industry-wide recommendations via various advocacy means but cannot unilaterally commit to them.

units.excerpt: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are a new requirement under our RSP. These will describe our concrete plans for making progress across Security, Alignment, Safeguards, and Policy.
units.paraphrase: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are introduced as a new requirement describing concrete plans across four domains.

units.excerpt: Goals described in the Roadmaps are intended to be ambitious, yet achievable—providing the kind of forcing function that we consider to be a past success of our RSP.
units.paraphrase: Roadmap goals are meant to be ambitious yet achievable, functioning as a forcing mechanism that has succeeded before.

units.excerpt: These are not hard commitments but rather public goals against which we will openly grade our progress.
units.paraphrase: Roadmap goals are public aspirations rather than binding commitments, with progress openly graded.

units.excerpt: Risk Reports are another new requirement. Risk Reports will provide detailed information on the safety profile of our models at the time of publication.
units.paraphrase: Risk Reports are introduced as a new requirement providing detailed safety-profile information at publication time.

units.excerpt: They will go beyond describing model capabilities, addressing our thinking on how capabilities, threat models (the specific ways that models might pose threats), and active risk mitigations fit together, providing an assessment of the overall level of risk.
units.paraphrase: Risk Reports will integrate capabilities, threat models, and mitigations into an overall risk assessment, beyond mere capability description.

units.excerpt: These reports will reflect our reasoning as to whether we believe the risks of training or deploying our models are justified by their corresponding benefits to the world.
units.paraphrase: Risk Reports will explain the reasoning behind whether training or deployment risks are justified by benefits.

units.excerpt: They will be published online, with some redactions to protect sensitive details about, for example, our training methods and organizations with whom we work.
units.paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published online with redactions protecting sensitive details like training methods and partner organizations.

units.excerpt: As detailed below, we also aim to subject Risk Reports to review by credible, independent external parties.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic aims to have Risk Reports reviewed by credible independent external parties.

units.excerpt: Finally, our governance commitments are intended to promote internal and external accountability, similar to those in our previous RSP.
units.paraphrase: Governance commitments aim to promote accountability, consistent with the prior RSP.

units.excerpt: Our RSP is only one part of our overall approach to safety. For instance, although this policy focuses on catastrophic risks, they are not the only risks we consider important—our Usage Policy and societal impacts research address other concerns.
units.paraphrase: The RSP is only part of Anthropic's safety approach, focused on catastrophic risks while other concerns are addressed elsewhere.

units.excerpt: Further, the RSP may serve some regulatory requirements, but it is not designed to be comprehensive. We want to keep it focused on our most central measures for addressing the catastrophic risks we prioritize most, rather than expand it to address every obligation we face.
units.paraphrase: The RSP is not meant to comprehensively meet regulatory requirements, but to stay focused on central catastrophic-risk measures.

units.excerpt: Where regulatory requirements exceed or differ from what the RSP covers, we will address them through separate documents.
units.paraphrase: Regulatory requirements beyond the RSP's scope will be addressed via separate documents.

units.excerpt: "Catastrophic risk" as used in our RSP refers generally to risks of the most severe potential harms from advanced AI, such as existential threats or fundamental destabilization of global systems. We use this term in its plain meaning rather than adopting any specific statutory definition.
units.paraphrase: Footnote 1 defines catastrophic risk in plain meaning terms rather than adopting a statutory definition.

units.excerpt: Where laws such as California SB 53 define this or similar terms with specific thresholds, we address those requirements in separate compliance frameworks.
units.paraphrase: Statutory definitions such as California SB 53's are addressed separately in compliance frameworks, not the RSP.

units.excerpt: This section outlines our recommendations for what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities. We lay this out in a three-column table.
units.paraphrase: Section 1 outlines industry-wide safety recommendations presented in a three-column table.

units.excerpt: The left column identifies capability thresholds that would call for heightened mitigations. The middle column provides an overview of our planned mitigations, which we have set forth more fully in our Frontier Safety Roadmap and other sections of this policy.
units.paraphrase: The table's left column lists capability thresholds; the middle column summarizes planned mitigations detailed elsewhere.

units.excerpt: The right column describes our recommendations for industry-wide safety at each threshold.
units.paraphrase: The right column of the table gives industry-wide safety recommendations per threshold.

units.excerpt: The distinction between our plans as a company (middle column) and our industry-wide recommendations (right column) reflects the limitations of any single AI developer's ability to ensure safety across the industry.
units.paraphrase: The company/industry-wide distinction reflects the limits of one developer's ability to secure industry-wide safety alone.

units.excerpt: In particular, we cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to staying in line with the industry-wide recommendations in the right column. However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
units.paraphrase: Anthropic cannot unconditionally commit to the industry-wide recommendations, but they will still shape important company work.

units.context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
units.excerpt: We use these recommendations as the north star for our risk mitigations planning as well as our public policy work. We will strive to advance these recommendations through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
units.paraphrase: The recommendations guide risk mitigation planning and public policy work, advanced through multiple advocacy channels.

units.context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
units.excerpt: We have also adopted a set of competitor-contingent commitments (see Appendix A) aimed at staying in line with these recommendations in scenarios where we can be confident that other relevant AI developers are doing the same.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic has adopted competitor-contingent commitments to align with the recommendations only when confident peers do likewise.

units.excerpt: At this point in AI's rapid development, we cannot presently give highly specific advance detail on what evaluations will determine whether risk thresholds have been passed, or what risk mitigations will be needed to achieve safety.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic cannot yet specify in advance the exact evaluations or mitigations needed given rapid AI development.

units.excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety are thus structured around requiring analysis and arguments making a strong case for safety, rather than AI Safety Levels (more in Appendix B).
units.paraphrase: The recommendations require safety-case arguments rather than fixed AI Safety Levels, detailed further in Appendix B.

units.excerpt: This leaves flexibility in how risk thresholds are evaluated and how safety is achieved and argued for. But it creates a challenge: one actor's view of what constitutes good risk assessment and mitigation may be very different from another's.
units.paraphrase: The flexible safety-case approach creates the challenge that different actors may hold very different views of adequate risk assessment.

units.excerpt: Ultimately, the best way for these recommendations to be implemented is likely via governance of all relevant frontier AI developers by third parties that determine which developers need to provide risk analyses and make arguments for the safety of their systems, and determine which such arguments are adequate.
units.paraphrase: Implementation is best achieved via third-party governance determining which developers must provide safety arguments and judging their adequacy.

units.excerpt: To the extent this takes the form of national regulation, different countries should attempt to harmonize their governance, including standards of evidence, to avoid a race to the bottom.
units.paraphrase: National regulations should be harmonized across countries, including evidentiary standards, to avoid a race to the bottom.

units.excerpt: In the shorter run, independent bodies (standards-setting organizations, auditors, etc.) might review such arguments and enforce high quality for private AI developers via voluntary mechanisms.
units.paraphrase: In the near term, independent bodies could review safety arguments and enforce quality via voluntary mechanisms.

units.excerpt: We expect that the recommendations for industry-wide safety will evolve significantly, as we learn more about AI capabilities, threat models, and risk mitigations. We hope these recommendations will become increasingly specific over time.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic expects the recommendations to evolve significantly and hopes they become more specific over time.

units.excerpt: Note that an AI developer might provide a single analysis covering a broad category of models, such that there isn't a new analysis needed for each release.
units.paraphrase: Footnote 2 notes a single analysis might cover a broad category of models rather than requiring per-release analysis.

units.excerpt: Additionally, determinations of which AI developers need to provide such analysis should be made with an effort to spare smaller AI developers from unnecessary compliance burden.
units.paraphrase: Footnote 2 also states smaller developers should be spared unnecessary compliance burden when determining analysis requirements.

units.locator: Table 1 / Non-novel chem/bio weapons production / Capability or usage threshold
units.context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Capability or usage threshold
units.excerpt: AI systems with the ability to significantly help individuals or groups with basic technical backgrounds (e.g., undergraduate STEM degrees) create/obtain and deploy chemical and/or biological weapons with serious potential for catastrophic damages.
units.paraphrase: This row defines the threshold as AI capable of substantially helping individuals with basic technical backgrounds create or deploy catastrophic chem/bio weapons.

units.locator: Table 1 / Non-novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-our plan as a company
units.context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company
units.excerpt: We will maintain or improve on our ASL-3 protections, which include classifier guards at least as robust as our initial Constitutional Classifiers; access controls for trusted users with exemptions to classifier guards; red-teaming, bug bounties, and threat intelligence for continually assessing the threat of jailbreaks; and a number of noteworthy security controls.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic commits to maintaining or improving ASL-3 protections including classifier guards, trusted-user access controls, red-teaming, bug bounties, and security controls.

units.locator: Table 1 / Non-novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-our plan as a company
units.context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company
units.excerpt: Specifics may change, but we will maintain equally or more robust measures over time and will publish updates in our Risk Reports.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain equal or greater protection robustness over time and report updates in Risk Reports.

units.locator: Table 1 / Non-novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-our plan as a company
units.context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company
units.excerpt: We expect to continuously meet the criteria in the right column, although we cannot make guarantees about an evolving landscape with continually adaptive attackers.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic expects to continuously meet the industry-wide criteria but cannot guarantee this given adaptive attackers.

units.locator: Table 1 / Non-novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that individual users and relatively small teams will not become significantly more likely to cause catastrophic harm via their usage of product surfaces or via theft of model weights. This will likely require:
units.paraphrase: The industry-wide recommendation is that developers argue individuals/small teams won't gain significantly increased ability to cause catastrophic harm via product use or weight theft.

units.locator: Table 1 / Non-novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
units.excerpt: Restrictions on model behavior, and/or measures for quickly detecting and acting on Usage Policy violations, accompanied by a strong case that these measures are difficult to reliably, sustainably circumvent via jailbreaking.
units.paraphrase: Recommended measures include behavioral restrictions or violation-detection, backed by an argument these are hard to jailbreak around.

units.locator: Table 1 / Non-novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 2
units.excerpt: Precautions against opportunistic theft of model weights, such as centralized controls on third-party applications and software updates.
units.paraphrase: Recommended measures include precautions against opportunistic weight theft, such as centralized controls on third-party apps and updates.

units.excerpt: This column summarizes commitments drawn from other sections of this policy and associated artifacts. It should be read as an overview, not as indicating any separate or additional plans.
units.paraphrase: Footnote 3 clarifies the middle column is a summary overview, not a source of additional commitments.

units.locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Capability or usage threshold
units.context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Capability or usage threshold
units.excerpt: AI systems with the ability to significantly help threat actors (for example, moderately resourced expert-backed teams) create/obtain and deploy chemical and/or biological weapons with potential for catastrophic damages far beyond those of past catastrophes such as COVID-19.
units.paraphrase: This row defines the threshold as AI substantially helping moderately resourced expert teams create weapons causing damage far exceeding COVID-19.

units.locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-our plan as a company
units.context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company
units.excerpt: We will apply protections at least as strong as our ASL-3 protections (see previous row) to an expanded set of potential use cases for AI, covering the most likely vectors for this threat.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will extend ASL-3-level protections to a broader set of use cases covering likely threat vectors.

units.locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-our plan as a company
units.context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company
units.excerpt: Additionally, we will identify the most concerning specific threat pathways, create policy recommendations for early detection and response for such threats, and share this content with policymakers.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will identify key threat pathways, create early-detection policy recommendations, and share these with policymakers.

units.locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that threat actors will not become significantly more likely to cause the sort of catastrophic harm discussed in the lefthand column via their usage of product surfaces or via theft of model weights.
units.paraphrase: The recommendation is that developers argue threat actors won't gain significantly increased ability to cause the described catastrophic harm.

units.locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those from the previous row, but to a higher standard—to the point where even well-resourced and -staffed threat actors would be unlikely to reliably jailbreak models or cause catastrophic harm via unauthorized access to or modification of models (including via stolen or modified model weights).
units.paraphrase: Similar measures are required but at a higher standard resisting even well-resourced threat actors from jailbreaking or misusing stolen weights.

units.locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: This would likely mean security roughly in line with RAND SL4, but it depends on the capabilities of the strongest and most plausible threat actors that are not bound by a credible governance regime enforcing the recommendations for industry-wide safety outlined here.
units.paraphrase: The recommended security level is roughly RAND SL4, contingent on the capabilities of the strongest unregulated threat actors.

units.locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Capability or usage threshold
units.context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Capability or usage threshold
units.excerpt: AI systems that are highly relied on and have extensive access to sensitive assets as well as moderate capacity for autonomous, goal-directed operation and subterfuge—such that it is plausible these AI systems could (if directed toward this goal, either deliberately or inadvertently) carry out sabotage leading to irreversibly and substantially higher odds of a later global catastrophe.
units.paraphrase: This row's threshold is AI with high reliance, sensitive-asset access, and moderate autonomous/subterfuge capacity plausibly able to cause sabotage raising catastrophe odds.

units.locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Capability or usage threshold
units.context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Capability or usage threshold
units.excerpt: In the near term, this possibility will likely be most applicable to AI systems that are extensively used within major AI companies, with the opportunity to manipulate how their successor systems are trained and deployed as well as the evidence used to assess their safety.
units.paraphrase: Near-term, this risk mainly applies to AI extensively used internally at major AI companies that could manipulate successor training or safety evidence.

units.locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Capability or usage threshold
units.context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Capability or usage threshold
units.excerpt: Down the line, this possibility may come to apply to AI systems deployed within government and other high-stakes settings.
units.paraphrase: Longer-term, this risk may extend to AI deployed in government and other high-stakes contexts.

units.locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Mitigations-our plan as a company
units.context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company
units.excerpt: We will detail the state of our AI systems' capabilities and propensities, our monitoring practices, and the overall level of risk in our Risk Reports.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will describe AI capabilities, propensities, monitoring practices, and overall risk level in Risk Reports.

units.locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Mitigations-our plan as a company
units.context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company
units.excerpt: We expect to continually be able to meet the criteria in the right column, although we cannot make guarantees about an evolving technology that may increasingly have the ability to detect and manipulate testing.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic expects to meet the right-column criteria continually but cannot guarantee this against tech that may learn to detect and manipulate testing.

units.context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that AI systems will not carry out sabotage leading to irreversibly and substantially higher odds of a later global catastrophe.
units.paraphrase: The recommendation is a strong argument that AI won't cause sabotage raising odds of later global catastrophe.

units.context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: This case may initially be relatively simple and rely heavily on capability limitations, if it is first required when the risk is merely plausible.
units.paraphrase: The safety case can initially be simple, relying on capability limits, if required only when the risk is merely plausible.

units.context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: As risk becomes harder to rule out, this case will likely include some combination of:
units.paraphrase: As risk becomes harder to rule out, the safety case will likely combine several elements listed below.

units.locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
units.context_stem: As risk becomes harder to rule out, this case will likely include some combination of:
units.excerpt: Internal compartmentalization, restriction, and code review to prevent excessive sabotage opportunities for AI models.
units.paraphrase: One recommended element is internal compartmentalization, restriction, and code review preventing sabotage opportunities.

units.locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 2
units.context_stem: As risk becomes harder to rule out, this case will likely include some combination of:
units.excerpt: Capability assessments demonstrating that AI models lack the ability to carry out irreversible (which would generally mean unnoticed) sabotage.
units.paraphrase: Another element is capability assessments showing models lack ability to carry out irreversible, unnoticed sabotage.

units.locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 3
units.context_stem: As risk becomes harder to rule out, this case will likely include some combination of:
units.excerpt: Monitoring and/or restricting AI behavior and usage internally.
units.paraphrase: Another element is internal monitoring and/or restriction of AI behavior and usage.

units.locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 4
units.context_stem: As risk becomes harder to rule out, this case will likely include some combination of:
units.excerpt: Evidence that AI models lack the propensity to deceive, manipulate, or sabotage users.
units.paraphrase: Another element is evidence showing models lack a propensity to deceive, manipulate, or sabotage users.

units.context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains; Column: Capability or usage threshold

units.paraphrase: This row's threshold is AI able to fully automate or dramatically accelerate top-tier research teams in domains threatening international security or global power balance.

units.context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains; Column: Capability or usage threshold
units.excerpt: For now, our evaluations will focus specifically on AI R&D, as this domain likely plays to AI systems' current strengths and is more tractable to assess than capabilities in other domains.
units.paraphrase: Evaluations currently focus on AI R&D since it suits current AI strengths and is more tractable to assess.

units.context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains; Column: Capability or usage threshold
units.excerpt: Additionally, AI R&D alone could cause acceleration in AI capabilities improvements, to the point where all of the threats listed above (and more) develop very quickly.
units.paraphrase: AI R&D acceleration alone could cause rapid development of all the other listed threats.

units.paraphrase: The operational trigger is a model capable of compressing two years of 2018-2024 AI progress into a single year.

units.context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains; Column: Capability or usage threshold
units.excerpt: This capability threshold is intended to reflect our definition of highly capable models (see Section 3.6). It may be sensible to add earlier, and/or easier-to-measure, thresholds that trigger less demanding versions of the mitigations for this threshold.
units.paraphrase: This threshold reflects the definition of highly capable models, and earlier easier-to-measure thresholds triggering lighter mitigations may be added.

units.locator: Table 1 / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations-our plan as a company / bullet 1
units.excerpt: Resource and complete significant "moonshot R&D for security" projects, to explore ambitious and possibly unconventional ways to achieve unprecedented levels of security against the world's best-resourced attackers.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will fund and complete ambitious moonshot security R&D projects seeking unprecedented protection against top attackers.

units.excerpt: Achieve an "eyes on everything" state for our internal AI development. We will comprehensively gather, centralize, and maintain logs for all critical AI-development activities, and use AI to analyze them for issues including security threats, concerning behavior by insiders (humans as well as AI systems themselves), and training processes or data that are out of line with the public Constitution that shapes and defines our AI models.

units.paraphrase: Anthropic will conduct systematic alignment assessments of Claude using mechanistic interpretability and adversarial red-teaming to test auditing methods.

units.paraphrase: Anthropic will develop internal red-teaming to outperform its bug bounty program participants at finding jailbreaks.

units.excerpt: Accomplishing this would likely mean security roughly in line with RAND SL4. Security requirements would be calibrated to defend against the strongest plausible threat actors who are not bound by a credible industry-wide safety regime.
units.paraphrase: This would require security roughly at RAND SL4, calibrated against the strongest unregulated threat actors.

units.locator: Table 1 / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: Actors subject to such a regime would not need to be treated as threats to each other's model weights.
units.paraphrase: Actors bound by a credible governance regime need not be treated as threats to each other's weights.

units.locator: Table 1 / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: Even malicious employees and other insiders with maximal levels of access will not be significantly enabled to cause catastrophic harm. This requires (among other things) accounting for internal tools that are less restricted than product surfaces, and for the possibility of unauthorized modification of models.
units.paraphrase: Recommendation includes ensuring even maximally-privileged malicious insiders cannot cause catastrophic harm, accounting for less-restricted internal tools and unauthorized model modification.

units.locator: Table 1 / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: This will likely require an internal Usage Policy and strong internal compartmentalization, controls and/or monitoring to restrict the ability of employees and contractors (up to and including the company's CEO as well as its most privileged technical employees) to circumvent the Usage Policy.
units.paraphrase: An internal Usage Policy with strong compartmentalization and controls is likely required, restricting even the CEO and most privileged employees from circumventing it.

units.locator: Table 1 / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: AI models have not been deliberately or inadvertently trained with dangerous goals, or are otherwise unlikely to autonomously cause catastrophic harm.
units.paraphrase: Recommendation includes ensuring models were not trained with dangerous goals and are unlikely to autonomously cause catastrophic harm.

units.locator: Table 1 / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those listed above under "High-stakes sabotage opportunities" (some combination of internal compartmentalization, restriction and code review; monitoring AI behavior; and evidence that AI models lack the propensity to deceive and manipulate users), but to a greater degree.
units.paraphrase: Similar measures to the sabotage row are needed, but to a greater degree.

units.locator: Table 1 / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
units.excerpt: In particular, at this point AI systems might be responsible for much of the research and analysis that underpins risk assessment, and might have strong capabilities for deception, manipulation and obfuscation of evidence, in which case analyses of threats from AIs should follow very high evidentiary standards with thorough and careful analysis of the possibility that much of the key evidence is suspect due to the possibility of manipulation by AI systems.
units.paraphrase: Because AI may underpin risk assessments and could deceive or obfuscate evidence, threat analyses should apply very high evidentiary standards accounting for possible AI manipulation of evidence.

units.excerpt: We will maintain a Frontier Safety Roadmap laying out ambitious but achievable goals for improving our risk mitigations—charting our progress as a company and raising the bar over time.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a Frontier Safety Roadmap of ambitious yet achievable goals, tracking progress and raising standards over time.

units.excerpt: Maintaining and reporting on this Roadmap is part of our work under the RSP. It will be shared with all full-time employees as well as our Board of Directors (Board) and Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), and published in redacted form.
units.paraphrase: Roadmap maintenance and reporting is part of RSP obligations; it will be shared internally with employees, the Board, and LTBT, and published in redacted form.

units.excerpt: We will provide updates on whether we achieve the goals, and set new goals when we do.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will report on goal achievement and set new goals upon achieving existing ones.

units.excerpt: Our Frontier Safety Roadmap is subject to change. Some changes may simply reflect our evolving understanding of how best to mitigate key risks.
units.paraphrase: The Roadmap may change, partly reflecting evolving understanding of risk mitigation.

units.excerpt: However, we will strive to avoid situations where we revise the goals in a less ambitious direction simply because we are unable to achieve them.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will try to avoid weakening goals merely due to inability to achieve them.

units.excerpt: By establishing this expectation, we hope to create a forcing function for work that would otherwise be challenging to appropriately prioritize and resource, as it requires collaboration (and in some cases sacrifices) from multiple parts of the company and can be at cross-purposes with immediate competitive and commercial priorities.
units.paraphrase: This expectation is meant to force prioritization of cross-company collaborative work that might otherwise conflict with commercial priorities.

units.excerpt: Publishing our Frontier Safety Roadmap may also help inform broader industry and policy discussions on AI safety.
units.paraphrase: Publishing the Roadmap may also contribute to broader industry and policy discussions.

units.excerpt: Our current Frontier Safety Roadmap is available at anthropic.com/responsible-scaling-policy/roadmap. We will also keep past Roadmaps available at that link.
units.paraphrase: The current Roadmap and past versions are published and kept available at a specified URL.

units.excerpt: We will publish Risk Reports discussing the risks of our systems and how we have made determinations about whether to continue AI development and deployment in light of the risks.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic commits to publishing Risk Reports covering system risks and the reasoning behind development and deployment decisions.

units.excerpt: These have significant content in common with system cards, but we are adding additional structure and process aimed at presenting our overall assessments of risk.
units.paraphrase: Risk Reports overlap with system cards but add extra structure and process for presenting overall risk assessments.

units.excerpt: Scope. A Risk Report will cover all publicly deployed models at the time of its publication.
units.paraphrase: Each Risk Report will include all models that are publicly deployed as of its publication date.

units.excerpt: It will also cover internally deployed models when we determine that these models could pose significant risks above and beyond those posed by our public models.
units.paraphrase: Internally deployed models will also be covered if they are judged to pose significant risks beyond those of public models.

units.excerpt: While there are a variety of reasons we might classify an internal model this way, this will—at a minimum—include any internal models that we are deploying for large-scale, fully autonomous research.
units.paraphrase: At minimum, internal models used for large-scale fully autonomous research will be classified as posing significant risk.

units.excerpt: Models fitting the above description are abbreviated below as "in-scope models."
units.paraphrase: Models meeting the described criteria are termed in-scope models for the rest of the document.

units.excerpt: We may also voluntarily include additional models in a Risk Report, e.g., to contribute to general discourse, but such inclusion does not expand the commitments below.
units.paraphrase: Additional models may be voluntarily included for discourse purposes without expanding the framework's commitments.

units.excerpt: Timing. We will publish a Risk Report every 3-6 months.
units.paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published on a 3-6 month cadence.

units.excerpt: Note that unlike system cards, Risk Reports will not be published with each new model release.
units.paraphrase: Unlike system cards, Risk Reports are not tied to individual model releases.

units.excerpt: When we publicly deploy a model that we determine is significantly more capable than any of the models covered in the most recent Risk Report, we will publish a discussion (in our System Card or elsewhere) of how that model's capabilities and propensities affect or change analysis in the Risk Report.
units.paraphrase: If a newly publicly deployed model is significantly more capable than any covered in the latest Risk Report, a discussion of its impact on the analysis will be published.

units.excerpt: Within 30 days of determining that we have an internally deployed model that is in-scope (per the description above), we will publish a discussion (in a System Card or elsewhere) of how that model's capabilities and propensities affect or change the analysis in the Risk Report.
units.paraphrase: Within 30 days of identifying an in-scope internal model, a discussion of its effect on the Risk Report analysis will be published.

units.excerpt: Specifically, risks arising from the capability thresholds in our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1).
units.paraphrase: The footnote clarifies that the significant risks referenced arise from capability thresholds described elsewhere in the industry-wide safety recommendations.

units.excerpt: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
units.paraphrase: Introductory lead-in to the list of guiding principles for Risk Reports.

units.context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
units.excerpt: We intend for our Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about how we see the risks of our systems and our state of preparedness for them.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic aims for Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about system risks and preparedness.

units.context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
units.excerpt: In particular, we will acknowledge when we view certain models as posing significant risks in absolute terms, even if our marginal contribution to overall ecosystem risk may be relatively limited when taking other developers' AI models into account.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will acknowledge significant absolute risks of its models regardless of its relatively smaller marginal contribution to industry-wide risk.

units.context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
units.excerpt: We will put significant effort into investigating (for example, via capability evaluations) the case for risk, and into sharing what we find.
units.paraphrase: Significant effort will go into investigating and sharing findings about the case for risk, including via capability evaluations.

units.context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
units.excerpt: When a Risk Report describes risk mitigations we have in place (or plan to implement shortly), we will keep our future practices in line with this description or track and report noteworthy changes and deviations (generally via subsequent Risk Reports).
units.paraphrase: Future practices will either match described mitigations or noteworthy deviations will be tracked and reported, typically in later Risk Reports.

units.context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
units.excerpt: We should make a strong attempt to ensure that ongoing (as opposed to temporary) changes do not significantly increase the level of risk.
units.paraphrase: A strong effort should be made to ensure ongoing changes do not meaningfully raise risk levels.

units.excerpt: Factual information. We will describe how we identify, evaluate, and mitigate catastrophic risks.
units.paraphrase: The factual information section will describe the processes for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating catastrophic risks.

units.excerpt: A Risk Report will document the following:
units.paraphrase: Lead-in sentence introducing the list of items a Risk Report must document.

units.context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
units.excerpt: Threat model identification: Our criteria for determining which catastrophic risks (i.e., threat models) we assess.
units.paraphrase: The report will document the criteria used to determine which catastrophic risks are assessed.

units.context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
units.excerpt: Threat model specification: The relevant threat models (which will, at a minimum, include those discussed above).
units.paraphrase: The report will specify relevant threat models, including at minimum those already discussed.

units.context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
units.excerpt: Evidence (including evaluations) about relevant model capabilities and behaviors: For each in-scope model, capability and alignment evaluations (conducted internally and by external parties as appropriate), their results, and (as appropriate) other evidence we considered in assessing the level of risk.
units.paraphrase: For each in-scope model, the report will present capability and alignment evaluations, their results, and other relevant evidence considered in the risk assessment.

units.context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
units.excerpt: Risk mitigations: For each in-scope model, the mitigations we are implementing across security, deployment safeguards, and alignment domains, along with discussion of their effectiveness.
units.paraphrase: For each in-scope model, mitigations across security, deployment safeguards, and alignment will be described along with their effectiveness.

units.context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
units.excerpt: Additional relevant factors: Any other considerations material to our risk analysis.
units.paraphrase: Any other material considerations relevant to the risk analysis will also be included.

units.excerpt: Risk analyses. We will provide our reasoning and conclusions regarding both specific threat models and overall risk levels.
units.paraphrase: The Risk Report will present reasoning and conclusions on both specific threat models and overall risk levels.

units.excerpt: Our analyses will include:
units.paraphrase: Lead-in sentence introducing the list of analysis components.

units.excerpt: Threat-specific risk assessment: For each threat model, we will analyze remaining absolute risk–i.e., the leftover risk after accounting for our mitigations.
units.paraphrase: For each threat model, the remaining absolute risk after mitigations will be analyzed.

units.excerpt: We will also discuss whether we believe we've crossed relevant thresholds in our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1), and (as relevant) whether we believe we're meeting the risk mitigation standards corresponding to them.
units.paraphrase: The report will also discuss whether relevant safety thresholds have been crossed and whether corresponding mitigation standards are being met.

units.excerpt: Overall risk assessment: We will provide an overall risk assessment.
units.paraphrase: An overall risk assessment will be provided.

units.excerpt: Risk-benefit determination: We will explain whether, and if so why, we believe the identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.
units.paraphrase: The report will explain whether and why identified risks are considered justified by corresponding benefits.

units.excerpt: Looking forward: We will outline our plans for continuing to monitor and mitigate the relevant risks over time.
units.paraphrase: Plans for continued monitoring and mitigation of risks over time will be outlined.

units.excerpt: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
units.paraphrase: Lead-in sentence introducing the list of topics addressed under review of past Risk Reports and decisions.

units.context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
units.excerpt: Changes in risk mitigation practices—noteworthy cases in which our risk mitigation practices deviated (including temporarily) or changed from what we discussed in our previous Risk Report over the relevant period, and their implications for the overall level of risk.
units.paraphrase: Noteworthy deviations or changes in risk mitigation practices since the previous Risk Report, and their risk implications, will be addressed.

units.context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
units.excerpt: Decisions to internally deploy in-scope models that would not otherwise be reviewed in a Risk Report (because they happened in between Risk Reports).
units.paraphrase: Decisions to internally deploy in-scope models between Risk Reports, which would otherwise go unreviewed, will be addressed.

units.context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
units.excerpt: We will discuss how these decisions were made and whether they appear reasonable in light of any noteworthy new information that has come to light since then.
units.paraphrase: The report will discuss how such internal deployment decisions were made and whether they remain reasonable given new information.

units.context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
units.excerpt: Changes to our Frontier Safety Roadmap and any cases where we failed to meet our goals.
units.paraphrase: Changes to the Frontier Safety Roadmap and any instances of failing to meet stated goals will be addressed.

units.excerpt: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis. If we determine that the absolute level of risk being imposed industry-wide by AI systems such as ours is high, and are justifying our decision to move forward based partly on a marginal risk analysis, we will additionally address the following:
units.paraphrase: If high industry-wide absolute risk is determined and a marginal risk analysis partly justifies moving forward, additional topics will be addressed.

units.context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis: we will additionally address the following:
units.excerpt: Competitive landscape analysis: What we know about how our current and future model capabilities and risk mitigations compare to those of relevant competitors.
units.paraphrase: The analysis will address knowledge about how current and future model capabilities and mitigations compare to competitors.

units.context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis: we will additionally address the following:
units.excerpt: Role in risk assessment: How these comparisons factored into our risk assessment.
units.paraphrase: How competitive comparisons factored into the overall risk assessment will be addressed.

units.context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis: we will additionally address the following:
units.excerpt: Benefits analysis: The benefits, if any, of continuing to maintain our existing models or of advancing frontier capabilities, including considerations related to our mission and our ability to contribute to AI safety research and policy development.
units.paraphrase: Benefits of continuing to maintain models or advance frontier capabilities, including mission-related considerations, will be analyzed.

units.context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis: we will additionally address the following:
units.excerpt: Advocacy efforts: The steps we took to raise public awareness of the relevant risks and to encourage appropriate regulatory action, including our engagement with policymakers and other AI developers.
units.paraphrase: Steps taken to raise public awareness and encourage regulatory action, including engagement with policymakers and other developers, will be described.

units.excerpt: We will conduct the assessments above with respect to each in-scope model.
units.paraphrase: All the described assessments will be conducted for each in-scope model.

units.excerpt: To avoid redundancy, we will likely analyze similar models collectively rather than individually, with appropriate justification for any such groupings.
units.paraphrase: Similar models will likely be analyzed collectively rather than individually to reduce redundancy, with justification for groupings.

units.excerpt: Initial assessment and drafting: Our internal subject matter experts will conduct risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.
units.paraphrase: Internal subject matter experts will conduct risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.

units.excerpt: Review and feedback: Separate internal reviewers will provide comprehensive feedback on the report, focusing on identifying potential methodological weaknesses, analytical gaps, or areas requiring additional evidence or clarification.
units.paraphrase: Separate internal reviewers will give comprehensive feedback focused on methodological weaknesses, analytical gaps, and areas needing more evidence or clarification.

units.excerpt: We will usually also seek feedback from trusted external parties with relevant expertise.
units.paraphrase: Feedback from trusted external experts will typically also be sought.

units.excerpt: Executive approval: The Risk Report, along with the internal feedback and any available external feedback, will be sent to the CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer (RSO) for final review and approval.
units.paraphrase: The Risk Report and accompanying feedback will be sent to the CEO and RSO for final review and approval.

units.excerpt: The CEO and RSO will make the ultimate determination regarding the adequacy of the risk assessment and any downstream deployment or development plans.
units.paraphrase: The CEO and RSO hold final decision authority over the adequacy of the risk assessment and any resulting deployment or development plans.

units.excerpt: Governance notification: Following approval of a Risk Report, the CEO and RSO will promptly share their decision(s), the underlying Risk Report, and internal feedback with both the Board and the LTBT.
units.paraphrase: After approval, the CEO and RSO will promptly share the decisions, the report, and internal feedback with the Board and the LTBT.

units.excerpt: Modified process when marginal risk analysis is important to our case. In the event that marginal risk analysis (see previous section) plays a major role in a decision to move forward, explicit approval of the Risk Report by the Board and LTBT (rather than just the CEO and RSO) will be required.
units.paraphrase: When marginal risk analysis plays a major role in a forward-moving decision, the Board and LTBT must explicitly approve the Risk Report instead of only the CEO and RSO.

units.excerpt: By "marginal risk analysis," we mean arguing that the risks imposed by our systems in particular are relatively lower when keeping in mind the risks unavoidably posed by other AI systems.
units.paraphrase: The footnote defines marginal risk analysis as arguing that a system's own risks are relatively lower given unavoidable risks from other AI systems.

units.excerpt: We will publish a public version of our Risk Report.
units.paraphrase: A public version of the Risk Report will be published.

units.excerpt: We will aim to minimize redactions to the public version of the report.
units.paraphrase: Redactions to the public version of the report will be minimized where possible.

units.excerpt: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
units.paraphrase: Lead-in sentence introducing the non-exhaustive list of reasons for redaction.

units.context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
units.excerpt: Legal compliance: To comply with legal obligations on disclosing information, such as export control regulations, national security restrictions, or contractual obligations with third parties.
units.paraphrase: Redaction may occur to comply with legal disclosure obligations such as export controls, national security restrictions, or third-party contracts.

units.context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
units.excerpt: Intellectual property protection: To protect proprietary information, including technical details of our models and training methodologies, trade secrets, or other confidential business information.
units.paraphrase: Redaction may occur to protect proprietary technical, methodological, or trade secret information.

units.context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
units.excerpt: Public safety considerations: To protect public safety by not disclosing information that could be exploited to cause harm.
units.paraphrase: Redaction may occur to prevent disclosure of information that could be exploited to cause harm.

units.context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
units.excerpt: Privacy: To protect the personal privacy of individuals.
units.paraphrase: Redaction may occur to protect individuals' personal privacy.

units.excerpt: We will work toward a practice of seeking comprehensive, public external review on our Risk Reports.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will work toward comprehensive, public external review of its Risk Reports.

units.excerpt: This means working with one or more third-party organizations that will receive private versions of our Risk Reports (unredacted or with minimal redactions, as discussed below) and publish comprehensive commentary on them.
units.paraphrase: This involves third-party organizations receiving largely unredacted private versions of the reports and publishing comprehensive commentary.

units.excerpt: Commentary will address topics including the quality of our reasoning, the validity of our risk assessments, the overall level of risk, and whether the redactions we've made for the public version are reasonable and appropriate.
units.paraphrase: External commentary will cover reasoning quality, risk assessment validity, overall risk level, and reasonableness of redactions.

units.excerpt: Our intent is for external reviewers' judgments to carry significant weight in the eyes of the public as well as our employees.
units.paraphrase: The intent is that external reviewers' judgments will carry significant weight with both the public and employees.

units.excerpt: But there are no well-established organizations or procedures for this sort of practice, and we are approaching it as an experiment.
units.paraphrase: No well-established organizations or procedures exist for this practice, so it is being approached experimentally.

units.excerpt: At a minimum, we will complete a full external review process (described below) with at least one external reviewer anytime a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted, defined as follows:
units.paraphrase: A full external review with at least one reviewer will be completed whenever a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted.

units.excerpt: A model is "highly capable" if we conclude it could fully automate, or dramatically accelerate, the work of large, top-tier research teams in domains where fast progress could threaten international security or rapidly disrupt the global balance of power—for example, energy, robotics, weapons development, or AI itself.
units.paraphrase: A model is deemed highly capable if it could fully automate or dramatically accelerate top research teams' work in domains that could threaten international security or disrupt the global balance of power.

units.excerpt: For now, our evaluations will focus specifically on AI R&D: we will consider a model highly capable if we determine that it could compress two years of 2018 – 2024 AI progress into a single year.
units.paraphrase: Evaluations currently focus on AI R&D, treating a model as highly capable if it could compress two years of 2018-2024 AI progress into one year.

units.excerpt: We hope to develop additional metrics for other domains over time. (The recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1) provide additional context.)
units.paraphrase: Additional metrics for other domains are hoped to be developed over time, with further context in the industry-wide safety recommendations.

units.excerpt: "Significantly redacted" means that the redactions omit information a reasonable external safety researcher would consider important in evaluating the overall level of risk, such that a reader of only the public version could not meaningfully assess whether they agree with our conclusions.
units.paraphrase: Significantly redacted means omitting information that a reasonable external safety researcher would deem important, preventing meaningful assessment by public-version readers.

units.excerpt: A report shall be deemed significantly redacted if, in the judgment of the RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT, it meets this description.
units.paraphrase: A report is deemed significantly redacted if the RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT judges it meets the definition.

units.excerpt: Note that unredacted reports will be shared with a large number of employees, who will be in a position to raise concerns if they believe the public version meets this description.
units.paraphrase: Unredacted reports will be shared broadly with employees, who can raise concerns if the public version appears significantly redacted.

units.excerpt: In consultation with the Board and LTBT, we will select external reviewers that:
units.paraphrase: Lead-in sentence introducing the criteria for selecting external reviewers, done in consultation with the Board and LTBT.

units.context_stem: In consultation with the Board and LTBT, we will select external reviewers that:
units.excerpt: Have significant experience and expertise regarding evaluations for dangerous AI capabilities and propensities.
units.paraphrase: Reviewers must have significant experience and expertise in evaluating dangerous AI capabilities and propensities.

units.context_stem: In consultation with the Board and LTBT, we will select external reviewers that:
units.excerpt: It's particularly important that they be knowledgeable about potential ways such evaluations might be misleading (for example, alignment faking).
units.paraphrase: Reviewers should particularly be knowledgeable about ways evaluations could be misleading, such as alignment faking.

units.context_stem: In consultation with the Board and LTBT, we will select external reviewers that:
units.excerpt: Have reputational and other incentives making them likely to be candid about their assessment of risks, rather than focused on writing comments that Anthropic will approve of.
units.paraphrase: Reviewers must have incentives to be candid about risk assessments rather than aiming to please Anthropic.

units.context_stem: In consultation with the Board and LTBT, we will select external reviewers that:
units.excerpt: For example, external review parties should not be teams whose revenue, reputation and success depend entirely on Anthropic and similar companies continuing to work with them.
units.paraphrase: External reviewers should not depend entirely on Anthropic or similar companies for their revenue, reputation, and success.

units.context_stem: In consultation with the Board and LTBT, we will select external reviewers that:
units.excerpt: Do not have conflicts of interest with respect to Anthropic. At a minimum, a reviewing organization itself may not have a financial interest in Anthropic;
units.paraphrase: Reviewers must have no conflicts of interest with Anthropic, and at minimum the reviewing organization itself may not hold a financial interest in Anthropic.

units.context_stem: In consultation with the Board and LTBT, we will select external reviewers that:
units.excerpt: and the individuals involved in conducting the review, as well as anyone above them in the reporting chain within their organization, may not have a financial interest in Anthropic or close personal relationships with anyone at Anthropic (i.e., family relationships, romantic relationships, or shared living arrangements).
units.paraphrase: Reviewing individuals and their organizational superiors must not have financial interests in Anthropic or close personal relationships with Anthropic staff.

units.excerpt: The external review process will involve sharing the Risk Report with one or more external reviewers within one week of submitting the same report to our Board and LTBT.
units.paraphrase: External reviewers will receive the Risk Report within one week of its submission to the Board and LTBT.

units.excerpt: We will ask the external reviewers to provide public commentary on our report within 30 days of receipt.
units.paraphrase: External reviewers will be asked to publish commentary within 30 days of receiving the report.

units.excerpt: We will try to work toward a process that involves the full external review being completed prior to Board/LTBT review (and may require this later).
units.paraphrase: Efforts will be made to complete full external review before Board/LTBT review, with this potentially becoming a firm requirement later.

units.excerpt: For purposes of external review, the only redactions to the Risk Report will be those necessary to comply with legal prohibitions or to maintain our legal rights.
units.paraphrase: For external review, redactions will be limited to those legally necessary or required to preserve legal rights.

units.excerpt: We expect that we will also invest some time in answering follow-up questions from parties doing external review.
units.paraphrase: Time is expected to be invested in answering follow-up questions from external reviewers.

units.excerpt: The external review will address:
units.paraphrase: Lead-in sentence introducing the list of topics the external review will cover.

units.excerpt: Adequacy of information: Whether the Risk Report contains sufficient information to assess the identified risks;
units.paraphrase: Reviewers will assess whether the report contains sufficient information to evaluate identified risks.

units.excerpt: Analytical rigor: The strength of the Risk Report's reasoning and analysis;
units.paraphrase: Reviewers will assess the strength of the report's reasoning and analysis.

units.excerpt: Areas of disagreement: Whether the external reviewer disagrees with any of the Risk Report's key claims and, if so, the reasons for any such disagreements; and
units.paraphrase: Reviewers will note any disagreements with key claims in the report and provide reasons.

units.excerpt: Risk reduction recommendations: Recommendations for further reducing identified risks.
units.paraphrase: Reviewers will provide recommendations for further reducing identified risks.

units.excerpt: The external reviewer will also evaluate our redaction decisions while avoiding disclosure of the redacted content itself.
units.paraphrase: Redaction decisions will also be evaluated by the external reviewer without disclosing the redacted content.

units.excerpt: In particular, the review will cover:
units.paraphrase: Lead-in sentence introducing the specific redaction-related review topics.

units.context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
units.excerpt: Redaction scope: The general nature and scope of redactions;
units.paraphrase: The review will cover the general nature and scope of redactions made.

units.context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
units.excerpt: Redaction justification: Whether the external reviewer generally agrees or disagrees with the publicly stated reasons for the redactions and, if relevant, the reasons for any disagreements;
units.paraphrase: The review will note whether the reviewer agrees with stated redaction justifications and, if not, why.

units.excerpt: For example, we may redact information if sharing it would endanger our legal right to treat it as confidential. This would be an uncommon situation.
units.paraphrase: The footnote gives an example: redaction may occur if disclosure would jeopardize the legal right to confidentiality, noting this would be uncommon.

units.excerpt: It does not mean we would redact information merely because it is sensitive or to reduce the risk of a leak.
units.paraphrase: The footnote clarifies that mere sensitivity or leak-risk reduction would not justify redaction.

units.context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
units.excerpt: Balancing test: Whether the redactions strike a reasonable balance between Anthropic's legitimate interests and society's interest in transparency; and
units.paraphrase: The review will assess whether redactions reasonably balance Anthropic's interests against society's interest in transparency.

units.context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:

units.paraphrase: The external reviewer will be asked to document its findings in a written report that is made public.

units.excerpt: External reviewers will be bound by obligations not to disclose confidential information (e.g., confidential intellectual property, matters of national security, or proprietary details such as model architecture, cost, or size), but beyond that will not be restricted in what they can publish, including concerns about the Risk Report or Anthropic's conduct in connection with the external review.

units.paraphrase: Anthropic commits to sharing complete, unredacted Risk Reports internally with regular-clearance staff.

units.excerpt: Noncompliance reporting: We will maintain a process for Anthropic staff to submit anonymous or identified reports regarding potential noncompliance with this policy.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a reporting process, allowing anonymous or identified submissions, for potential policy noncompliance.

units.excerpt: Staff will have more than one option for who receives these reports, including the RSO, and at least one executive who does not report to the RSO.
units.paraphrase: Staff can choose among multiple report recipients, including the RSO and an executive independent of the RSO.

units.excerpt: When we receive a report, we will promptly investigate, take appropriate and proportional corrective action if it is substantiated, and document the report and our findings.
units.paraphrase: Upon receiving a report, Anthropic will investigate promptly, act proportionally if substantiated, and document the outcome.

units.paraphrase: Anthropic will give the Board quarterly updates on all noncompliance reports regardless of substantiation.

units.paraphrase: Anthropic will not use non-disparagement contract terms that could discourage employees from raising safety concerns publicly.

units.paraphrase: Any non-disparagement clause offered will still permit raising safety concerns and disclosing the clause's existence.
