units.excerpt: RSP-2023 (aka RSP v1.0): Initial version.
units.paraphrase: The changelog entry marks the initial RSP version from September 2023.

units.excerpt: RSP-2024: This update introduces a more flexible and nuanced approach to assessing and managing AI risks while maintaining our commitment not to train or deploy models unless we have implemented adequate safeguards.
units.paraphrase: The 2024 update adopts a more flexible risk-management approach while preserving the core commitment on adequate safeguards.

units.excerpt: Key improvements include new capability thresholds to indicate when we should upgrade our safeguards, refined processes for evaluating model capabilities and the adequacy of our safeguards (inspired by safety case methodologies), and new measures for internal governance and external input.
units.paraphrase: Key improvements include new capability thresholds, refined evaluation processes inspired by safety cases, and new governance and external-input measures.

units.excerpt: We describe the most notable changes below.
units.paraphrase: The document notes that the most significant changes follow.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ASL definition changed
units.excerpt: ASL definition changed: The term "ASL" now refers to groups of technical and operational safeguards (it previously also referred to models).
units.paraphrase: The changelog notes ASL now denotes safeguard groups only, not models as before.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ASL definition changed
units.excerpt: We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards. This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
units.paraphrase: New Capability Threshold and Required Safeguard concepts allow safeguards to be applied more precisely to specific capabilities rather than broad categories.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
units.excerpt: ARA threshold now a checkpoint: We replaced our previous autonomous replication and adaption (ARA) threshold with a "checkpoint" for autonomous AI capabilities.
units.paraphrase: The prior ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint concept for autonomous AI capabilities.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
units.excerpt: Rather than triggering higher safety standards automatically, reaching this checkpoint will prompt additional evaluation of the model's capabilities and accelerate our preparation of stronger safeguards.
units.paraphrase: Reaching the checkpoint prompts further evaluation and accelerated safeguard preparation rather than automatically triggering higher standards.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
units.excerpt: We previously considered these capabilities as a trigger for increased safeguards, motivated by an attempt to establish some threshold while we developed a better sense of potential threats.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic explains the earlier trigger reflected an attempt to set a threshold before threats were well understood.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
units.excerpt: We now believe that these capabilities - at the levels we initially considered - would not necessitate the ASL-3 standard.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic now judges that the initially considered capability levels do not require ASL-3.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / AI R&D threshold added
units.excerpt: AI R&D threshold added: We added a new threshold for AI systems that can significantly advance AI development.
units.paraphrase: A new threshold was added for AI systems capable of significantly advancing AI development.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / AI R&D threshold added
units.excerpt: Such capabilities could lead to rapid, unpredictable advances in AI, potentially outpacing our ability to evaluate and address emerging risks, and may also serve as an early warning sign for the ability to automate R&D in other domains.
units.paraphrase: Such capabilities risk rapid unpredictable AI progress outpacing risk evaluation, and may signal broader R&D automation ability.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
units.excerpt: Testing for Capability Thresholds: Rather than using prespecified evaluations, we now require an affirmative case that models are sufficiently far from Capability Thresholds.
units.paraphrase: Instead of fixed evaluations, an affirmative case is now required showing sufficient distance from Capability Thresholds.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
units.excerpt: Predefined tests may miss emerging risks or be overly conservative relative to the actual threshold of concern.
units.paraphrase: Fixed tests risk missing new risks or being overly cautious relative to the real threshold of concern.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
units.excerpt: Our most accurate tests change frequently enough that it is more practical to use this new approach than to have our Board pre-approve evaluations.
units.paraphrase: Because accurate tests change often, the new approach is more practical than requiring Board pre-approval of evaluations.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Adjusted evaluation cadence
units.excerpt: Adjusted evaluation cadence: We adjusted the comprehensive assessment cadence to 4x Effective Compute or six months of accumulated post-training enhancements (this was previously three months).
units.paraphrase: The comprehensive assessment cadence was changed to 4x Effective Compute or six months of post-training enhancements, up from three months.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Adjusted evaluation cadence
units.excerpt: We found that a three-month cadence forced teams to prioritize conducting frequent evaluations over more comprehensive testing and improving methodologies.
units.paraphrase: The three-month cadence had forced teams to favor evaluation frequency over thoroughness and methodological improvement.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
units.excerpt: Less prescriptive evaluation methodology: We have replaced some specifics in our previous testing methodology (e.g., using 1% of compute for elicitation or creating a 6x buffer), with more general requirements to (a) match expected efforts of potential adversaries and (b) provide informal estimates of how further scaling and research developments will impact model capabilities and performance on the same tasks.
units.paraphrase: Specific prior methodology figures, such as 1% compute for elicitation or a 6x buffer, were replaced with general requirements to match adversary effort and estimate scaling impacts.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
units.excerpt: We have found that specific methodologies may become outdated when new research developments are introduced.
units.paraphrase: Specific methodologies risk becoming outdated as new research emerges.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
units.excerpt: Although still an aspirational goal, the science of evaluations is not currently mature enough to make confident predictions about the precise buffer we should require between current models and a Capability Threshold.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic notes evaluation science remains too immature to confidently specify the precise buffer needed before a Capability Threshold, though this remains an aspiration.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements

units.paraphrase: ASL-3 safeguard requirements were updated to be less prescriptive and more focused on outcomes.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
units.excerpt: Rather than detailing specific operational and technical safeguards, we now specify the overall security or deployment standards and requirements for meeting them.
units.paraphrase: Instead of listing specific controls, overall standards and the requirements to meet them are now specified.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
units.excerpt: This is to allow us to adapt our safeguards more flexibly as our understanding of risks and possible safeguards improves.
units.paraphrase: The change aims to enable more flexible adaptation of safeguards as understanding improves.

units.paraphrase: The ASL-2 Security standard no longer includes commitments to protect against scaled or distillation attacks.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
units.excerpt: While distillation remains a concern for more capable models, models stored under ASL-2 safeguards have not yet reached potentially harmful Capability Thresholds.
units.paraphrase: Distillation is still a concern for more capable models, but ASL-2-safeguarded models have not reached potentially harmful thresholds.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
units.excerpt: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users: We have updated the ASL-3 Deployment Standard to allow for different levels of safeguards based on deployment context.
units.paraphrase: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard now allows varying safeguard levels depending on deployment context.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
units.excerpt: For any general access systems, we still require passing intensive red-teaming.
units.paraphrase: General access systems must still pass intensive red-teaming.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users

units.paraphrase: For internal use, safety testing, or deployment to sufficiently trusted users, access controls and monitoring are required instead.

units.excerpt: New Capability and Safeguards Reports: We have introduced Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports.
units.paraphrase: New Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports were introduced.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / New Capability and Safeguards Reports

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Internal and external accountability

units.paraphrase: Several changes were made to the previous procedural commitments.

units.excerpt: These include expanding the duties of the Responsible Scaling Officer; adding internal critique and external expert input on capability and safeguard assessments; new procedures related to internal governance; and maintaining a public page for overviews of past Capability and Safeguard Reports, RSP-related updates, and future plans.
units.paraphrase: Changes include expanded RSO duties, added internal critique and external expert input, new internal governance procedures, and a public page summarizing reports, updates and plans.

units.excerpt: RSP-2025: This update clarifies which Capability Thresholds would require enhanced safeguards beyond our current ASL-3 standards.
units.paraphrase: The 2025 update clarifies which Capability Thresholds require safeguards beyond current ASL-3 standards.

units.excerpt: The key changes include:

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.1 / New Capability Thresholds
units.excerpt: New Capability Thresholds: We have added a new capability threshold related to CBRN development, which defines capabilities that could substantially uplift the development capabilities of moderately resourced state programs.
units.paraphrase: A new CBRN-related capability threshold was added, defined by potential to substantially uplift moderately resourced state programs.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.1 / New Capability Thresholds
units.excerpt: We have also disaggregated our existing AI R&D capability thresholds, separating them into two distinct levels (the ability to fully automate entry-level AI research work, and the ability to cause dramatic acceleration in the rate of effective scaling) and provided additional detail on the corresponding Required Safeguards.
units.paraphrase: AI R&D thresholds were split into two levels—full automation of entry-level research and dramatic acceleration of effective scaling—with more detail on corresponding safeguards.

units.excerpt: Iterative Commitment: We have adopted a general commitment to reevaluate our Capability Thresholds whenever we upgrade to a new set of Required Safeguards.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic commits to reassessing Capability Thresholds each time Required Safeguards are upgraded.

units.excerpt: We have decided not to maintain a commitment to define ASL-N+1 evaluations by the time we develop ASL-N models; such an approach would add unnecessary complexity because Capability Thresholds do not naturally come grouped in discrete levels.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic dropped the commitment to predefine next-level evaluations before reaching the current level, since thresholds don't naturally fall into discrete levels.

units.excerpt: We believe it is more practical and sensible instead to commit to reconsidering the whole list of Capability Thresholds whenever we upgrade our safeguards.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic prefers reconsidering the entire list of thresholds together whenever safeguards are upgraded.

units.excerpt: ASL-3 Security: This update excludes both sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders from the ASL-3 Security Standard.
units.paraphrase: The 2.2 update excludes sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders from ASL-3 Security Standard scope.

units.excerpt: Previously, only "highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders" were explicitly excluded.
units.paraphrase: Previously the exclusion covered only highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders.

units.excerpt: The model capabilities and threat models corresponding with the ASL-3 Security Standard do not warrant protection against either group: the CBRN-3 threat models entail large numbers of users having access to unguarded models (which is more likely to occur through a universal jailbreak than via model theft), and the relatively small number of employees who might be capable of model theft does not significantly affect the risk level.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic reasons that ASL-3 threat models, particularly CBRN-3, are more about jailbreaks than model theft, so excluding these insider groups does not meaningfully raise risk.

units.excerpt: For AI R&D-4, the threat models generally do not depend on model weight theft and instead entail AI systems engaging in autonomous internal sabotage.
units.paraphrase: For AI R&D-4, threat models focus on autonomous internal sabotage rather than weight theft.

units.excerpt: This update is a comprehensive rewrite of our RSP.
units.paraphrase: The 2026 update represents a full rewrite of the RSP.

units.excerpt: For a summary of changes and the thinking behind them, see here.
units.paraphrase: A separate summary of changes and rationale is referenced externally.

excerpt: Our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) is our voluntary framework for managing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems.
paraphrase: The RSP is described as a voluntary framework for managing catastrophic AI risk.

excerpt: It establishes how we identify and evaluate risks, how we make decisions about AI development and deployment, and, from the perspective of the world at large, how we aim to make sure that the benefits of our models exceed their costs.
paraphrase: The RSP covers risk identification, development/deployment decisions, and ensuring benefits exceed costs from a societal perspective.

excerpt: We have always intended for our RSP to be a living document.
paraphrase: The RSP is intended to be a living document.

excerpt: We will continually update the RSP as we learn more about AI capabilities and risks, develop and refine technical safety measures, and gain more experience navigating an ecosystem in which the risks to society depend on the actions of many developers.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to continually updating the RSP as understanding of capabilities, risks, safety measures, and multi-developer dynamics improves.

excerpt: The major components of this third iteration are as follows:
paraphrase: This introduces a list of the major components of the third RSP iteration.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety outline what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The document introduces industry-wide safety recommendations aimed at keeping catastrophic risk low during rapid AI advances.

excerpt: We lay this out in a table that maps capability thresholds to the mitigations we believe they call for.
paraphrase: A table maps capability thresholds to corresponding mitigations.

excerpt: We also include our planned mitigations as a company, which are drawn from other sections of this policy and associated artifacts.
paraphrase: Company-specific planned mitigations, sourced from elsewhere in the policy, are also included.

excerpt: This approach represents a change from our previous RSP, driven by a collective action problem.
paraphrase: The new approach reflects a change from the prior RSP due to a collective action problem.

excerpt: The overall level of catastrophic risk from AI depends on the actions of multiple AI developers, not just one.
paraphrase: Catastrophic risk depends on the collective actions of multiple AI developers.

excerpt: Our previous RSP committed to implementing mitigations that would reduce our models' absolute risk levels to acceptable levels, without regard to whether other frontier AI developers would do the same.
paraphrase: The prior RSP focused on reducing absolute risk regardless of other developers' actions.

excerpt: But from a societal perspective, what matters is the risk to the ecosystem as a whole.
paraphrase: From a societal standpoint, ecosystem-wide risk is what matters.

excerpt: If one AI developer paused development to implement safety measures while others moved forward with training and deploying AI systems without strong mitigations, that could result in a world that is less safe—the developers with the weakest protections would set the pace, and responsible developers would lose their ability to do safety research and advance the public benefit.
paraphrase: Unilateral pausing by one developer while others proceed unsafely could make the world less safe overall.

excerpt: Although this situation has not yet arisen, it looks likely enough that we want to prepare for it.
paraphrase: This scenario has not occurred but seems likely enough to warrant preparation.

excerpt: We now separate our plans as a company—those which we expect to achieve regardless of what any other company does—from our more ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
paraphrase: Company-specific plans are now separated from broader industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: We aspire to advance the latter through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
paraphrase: Anthropic aspires to advance industry-wide recommendations through example-setting, technical work, and advocacy.

excerpt: But we cannot commit to following them unilaterally.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot unilaterally commit to the industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are a new requirement under our RSP.
paraphrase: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are introduced as a new RSP requirement.

excerpt: These will describe our concrete plans for making progress across Security, Alignment, Safeguards, and Policy.
paraphrase: The Roadmaps will describe concrete plans across four domains: Security, Alignment, Safeguards, and Policy.

excerpt: Goals described in the Roadmaps are intended to be ambitious, yet achievable—providing the kind of forcing function that we consider to be a past success of our RSP.
paraphrase: Roadmap goals are meant to be ambitious yet achievable, functioning as a forcing mechanism that has worked well previously.

excerpt: These are not hard commitments but rather public goals against which we will openly grade our progress.
paraphrase: Roadmap goals are not binding commitments but public benchmarks for self-assessment.

excerpt: Risk Reports are another new requirement. Risk Reports will provide detailed information on the safety profile of our models at the time of publication.
paraphrase: Risk Reports are introduced as a new requirement providing detailed safety-profile information at publication time.

excerpt: They will go beyond describing model capabilities, addressing our thinking on how capabilities, threat models (the specific ways that models might pose threats), and active risk mitigations fit together, providing an assessment of the overall level of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will integrate capabilities, threat models, and mitigations into an overall risk assessment.

excerpt: These reports will reflect our reasoning as to whether we believe the risks of training or deploying our models are justified by their corresponding benefits to the world.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will explain whether the risks of training/deploying models are justified by their benefits.

excerpt: They will be published online, with some redactions to protect sensitive details about, for example, our training methods and organizations with whom we work.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published online with redactions of sensitive information.

excerpt: As detailed below, we also aim to subject Risk Reports to review by credible, independent external parties.
paraphrase: Risk Reports are also intended to undergo review by credible independent external parties.

excerpt: Finally, our governance commitments are intended to promote internal and external accountability, similar to those in our previous RSP.
paraphrase: Governance commitments aim to promote accountability, consistent with the prior RSP.

excerpt: Our RSP is only one part of our overall approach to safety.
paraphrase: The RSP is only one component of the broader safety approach.

excerpt: For instance, although this policy focuses on catastrophic risks, they are not the only risks we consider important—our Usage Policy and societal impacts research address other concerns.
paraphrase: Other risks beyond catastrophic risk are addressed by the Usage Policy and societal impacts research.

excerpt: Further, the RSP may serve some regulatory requirements, but it is not designed to be comprehensive.
paraphrase: The RSP may partially fulfill regulatory requirements but is not intended as a comprehensive compliance document.

excerpt: We want to keep it focused on our most central measures for addressing the catastrophic risks we prioritize most, rather than expand it to address every obligation we face.
paraphrase: The RSP is deliberately kept focused on core catastrophic-risk measures rather than every obligation.

excerpt: Where regulatory requirements exceed or differ from what the RSP covers, we will address them through separate documents.
paraphrase: Additional or differing regulatory requirements will be addressed in separate documents.

excerpt: "Catastrophic risk" as used in our RSP refers generally to risks of the most severe potential harms from advanced AI, such as existential threats or fundamental destabilization of global systems.
paraphrase: Catastrophic risk is defined broadly as the most severe potential harms, including existential threats or global destabilization.

excerpt: We use this term in its plain meaning rather than adopting any specific statutory definition.
paraphrase: The term is used in its plain meaning, not tied to a specific statutory definition.

excerpt: Where laws such as California SB 53 define this or similar terms with specific thresholds, we address those requirements in separate compliance frameworks.
paraphrase: Legal definitions such as those in California SB 53 are addressed via separate compliance frameworks.

excerpt: This section outlines our recommendations for what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: This section presents recommendations for industry-wide safety during rapid AI capability growth.

excerpt: We lay this out in a three-column table.
paraphrase: The recommendations are presented in a three-column table.

excerpt: The left column identifies capability thresholds that would call for heightened mitigations.
paraphrase: The left column of the table lists capability thresholds triggering heightened mitigations.

excerpt: The middle column provides an overview of our planned mitigations, which we have set forth more fully in our Frontier Safety Roadmap and other sections of this policy.
paraphrase: The middle column summarizes company mitigations detailed elsewhere in the policy and Roadmap.

excerpt: The right column describes our recommendations for industry-wide safety at each threshold.
paraphrase: The right column contains industry-wide safety recommendations for each threshold.

excerpt: The distinction between our plans as a company (middle column) and our industry-wide recommendations (right column) reflects the limitations of any single AI developer's ability to ensure safety across the industry.
paraphrase: The company/industry-wide distinction reflects limits on a single developer's ability to ensure industry-wide safety.

excerpt: In particular, we cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to staying in line with the industry-wide recommendations in the right column.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot unconditionally commit unilaterally to the right-column recommendations.

excerpt: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
paraphrase: The recommendations will nonetheless shape important aspects of Anthropic's work.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We use these recommendations as the north star for our risk mitigations planning as well as our public policy work.
paraphrase: The recommendations serve as the guiding standard for risk mitigation planning and public policy work.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We will strive to advance these recommendations through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will try to advance these recommendations through example-setting, technical work, and advocacy.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We have also adopted a set of competitor-contingent commitments (see Appendix A) aimed at staying in line with these recommendations in scenarios where we can be confident that other relevant AI developers are doing the same.
paraphrase: Anthropic has adopted commitments contingent on competitors' behavior, detailed in Appendix A.

excerpt: At this point in AI's rapid development, we cannot presently give highly specific advance detail on what evaluations will determine whether risk thresholds have been passed, or what risk mitigations will be needed to achieve safety.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot currently specify detailed evaluations for risk thresholds or the mitigations safety would require.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety are thus structured around requiring analysis and arguments making a strong case for safety, rather than AI Safety Levels (more in Appendix B).
paraphrase: Recommendations are built around requiring safety-case arguments rather than fixed AI Safety Levels.

excerpt: This leaves flexibility in how risk thresholds are evaluated and how safety is achieved and argued for.
paraphrase: The safety-case approach allows flexibility in evaluating thresholds and achieving/arguing safety.

excerpt: But it creates a challenge: one actor's view of what constitutes good risk assessment and mitigation may be very different from another's.
paraphrase: This flexibility creates a challenge since different actors may hold very different standards for adequate risk assessment.

excerpt: Ultimately, the best way for these recommendations to be implemented is likely via governance of all relevant frontier AI developers by third parties that determine which developers need to provide risk analyses and make arguments for the safety of their systems, and determine which such arguments are adequate.
paraphrase: Implementation is best achieved through third-party governance determining which developers must provide risk analyses and assessing their adequacy.

excerpt: To the extent this takes the form of national regulation, different countries should attempt to harmonize their governance, including standards of evidence, to avoid a race to the bottom.
paraphrase: National regulations should be harmonized across countries to prevent a race to the bottom.

excerpt: In the shorter run, independent bodies (standards-setting organizations, auditors, etc.) might review such arguments and enforce high quality standards for private AI developers via voluntary mechanisms.
paraphrase: In the near term, independent bodies could review safety arguments and enforce quality standards voluntarily.

excerpt: We expect that the recommendations for industry-wide safety will evolve significantly, as we learn more about AI capabilities, threat models, and risk mitigations.
paraphrase: The industry-wide recommendations are expected to evolve significantly as understanding improves.

excerpt: We hope these recommendations will become increasingly specific over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic hopes the recommendations will grow more specific over time.

excerpt: Note that an AI developer might provide a single analysis covering a broad category of models, such that there isn't a new analysis needed for each release.
paraphrase: A single analysis could cover a broad category of models rather than requiring one per release.

excerpt: Additionally, determinations of which AI developers need to provide such analysis should be made with an effort to spare smaller AI developers from unnecessary compliance burden.
paraphrase: Determinations of which developers must provide analysis should try to spare smaller developers unnecessary compliance burden.

excerpt: In particular, at this point AI systems might be responsible for much of the research and analysis that underpins risk assessment, and might have strong capabilities for deception, manipulation and obfuscation of evidence, in which case analyses of threats from AIs should follow very high evidentiary standards with thorough and careful analysis of the possibility that much of the key evidence is suspect due to the possibility of manipulation by AI systems.
paraphrase: Because AI may underpin risk-assessment research and could have strong deceptive capabilities, threat analyses should apply very high evidentiary standards accounting for possible evidence manipulation.

excerpt: We will maintain a Frontier Safety Roadmap laying out ambitious but achievable goals for improving our risk mitigations—charting our progress as a company and raising the bar over time.
paraphrase: The Frontier Safety Roadmap will set ambitious, achievable risk-mitigation goals and track progress over time.

excerpt: Maintaining and reporting on this Roadmap is part of our work under the RSP.
paraphrase: Maintaining and reporting the Roadmap is part of RSP obligations.

excerpt: It will be shared with all full-time employees as well as our Board of Directors (Board) and Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), and published in redacted form.
paraphrase: The Roadmap will be shared internally with employees, the Board, and the LTBT, and published externally in redacted form.

excerpt: We will provide updates on whether we achieve the goals, and set new goals when we do.
paraphrase: Anthropic will report on goal achievement and set new goals as prior ones are met.

excerpt: Our Frontier Safety Roadmap is subject to change.
paraphrase: The Roadmap may change over time.

excerpt: Some changes may simply reflect our evolving understanding of how best to mitigate key risks.
paraphrase: Changes to the Roadmap may reflect evolving understanding of risk mitigation.

excerpt: However, we will strive to avoid situations where we revise the goals in a less ambitious direction simply because we are unable to achieve them.
paraphrase: Anthropic will try to avoid weakening goals merely because they proved hard to achieve.

excerpt: By establishing this expectation, we hope to create a forcing function for work that would otherwise be challenging to appropriately prioritize and resource, as it requires collaboration (and in some cases sacrifices) from multiple parts of the company and can be at cross-purposes with immediate competitive and commercial priorities.
paraphrase: This expectation is meant to force prioritization of cross-company collaborative work that competes with commercial priorities.

excerpt: Publishing our Frontier Safety Roadmap may also help inform broader industry and policy discussions on AI safety.
paraphrase: Publishing the Roadmap could contribute to wider industry and policy discussions on AI safety.

excerpt: Our current Frontier Safety Roadmap is available at anthropic.com/responsible-scaling-policy/roadmap.
paraphrase: The current Roadmap is published at a specified URL.

excerpt: We will also keep past Roadmaps available at that link.
paraphrase: Past Roadmap versions will remain available at the same link.

excerpt: We will publish Risk Reports discussing the risks of our systems and how we have made determinations about whether to continue AI development and deployment in light of the risks.
paraphrase: Anthropic will publish Risk Reports that discuss system risks and the determinations made about continuing AI development and deployment.

excerpt: These have significant content in common with system cards, but we are adding additional structure and process aimed at presenting our overall assessments of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports overlap with system cards but include added structure and process for presenting overall risk assessments.

excerpt: A Risk Report will cover all publicly deployed models at the time of its publication.
paraphrase: Each Risk Report will cover all models publicly deployed as of its publication date.

excerpt: It will also cover internally deployed models when we determine that these models could pose significant risks beyond those posed by models that are covered by a prior Risk Report.
paraphrase: Internally deployed models will also be covered if they are judged to pose significant risks not already addressed in a prior Risk Report.

excerpt: While there are a variety of reasons we might classify an internal model this way, this will—at a minimum—include any internal models that we are deploying for large-scale, fully autonomous research.
paraphrase: At minimum, internal models used for large-scale fully autonomous research will be classified as posing significant risk.

excerpt: Models fitting the above description are abbreviated below as "in-scope models."
paraphrase: Models meeting the described criteria are termed "in-scope models" in the document.

excerpt: We may also voluntarily include additional models in a Risk Report, e.g., to contribute to general discourse, but such inclusion does not expand the commitments below.
paraphrase: Additional models may be voluntarily included in a Risk Report without expanding the stated commitments.

excerpt: We will publish a Risk Report every 3-6 months.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published on a 3-6 month cadence.

excerpt: Note that unlike system cards, Risk Reports will not be published with each new model release.
paraphrase: Unlike system cards, Risk Reports are not tied to each new model release.

excerpt: When we publicly deploy a model that we determine is significantly more capable than any of the models covered in the most recent Risk Report, we will publish a discussion (in our System Card or elsewhere) of how that model's capabilities and propensities affect or change analysis in the Risk Report.
paraphrase: If a newly publicly deployed model is significantly more capable than any model in the latest Risk Report, a discussion of its impact on the analysis will be published.

excerpt: Within 30 days of determining that we have an internally deployed model that is in-scope (per the description above), we will publish a discussion (in a System Card or elsewhere) of how that model's capabilities and propensities affect or change the analysis in the Risk Report.
paraphrase: Within 30 days of identifying an in-scope internally deployed model, a discussion of its effect on the Risk Report analysis will be published.

excerpt: Specifically, risks arising from the capability thresholds in our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1).
paraphrase: The footnote clarifies that significant risks refer to those arising from capability thresholds in the industry-wide safety recommendations.

excerpt: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
paraphrase: The section introduces guiding principles for Risk Reports.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We intend for our Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about how we see the risks of our systems and our state of preparedness for them.
paraphrase: Risk Reports are intended to be direct, candid, and informative regarding risk perception and preparedness.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: In particular, we will acknowledge when we view certain models as posing significant risks in absolute terms, even if our marginal contribution to overall ecosystem risk may be relatively limited when taking other developers' AI models into account.
paraphrase: Significant absolute risks of certain models will be acknowledged even when Anthropic's marginal contribution to ecosystem risk is limited.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We will put significant effort into investigating (for example, via capability evaluations) the case for risk, and into sharing what we find.
paraphrase: Significant effort will be invested in investigating the case for risk and sharing findings.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: When a Risk Report describes risk mitigations we have in place (or plan to implement shortly), we will keep our future practices in line with this description or track and report noteworthy changes and deviations (generally via subsequent Risk Reports).
paraphrase: Future practices will either match described mitigations or noteworthy deviations will be tracked and reported in later Risk Reports.

context_stem: When a Risk Report describes risk mitigations we have in place...
excerpt: We should make a strong attempt to ensure that ongoing (as opposed to temporary) changes do not significantly increase the level of risk.
paraphrase: A strong effort should be made to ensure ongoing changes do not meaningfully raise risk levels.

excerpt: We will describe how we identify, evaluate, and mitigate catastrophic risks.
paraphrase: The report will describe the process of identifying, evaluating, and mitigating catastrophic risks.

excerpt: A Risk Report will document the following:
paraphrase: The following items will be documented in a Risk Report.

context_stem: Factual information. A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Threat model identification: Our criteria for determining which catastrophic risks (i.e., threat models) we assess.
paraphrase: The report will state the criteria used to determine which catastrophic risk threat models are assessed.

context_stem: Factual information. A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Threat model specification: The relevant threat models (which will, at a minimum, include those discussed above).
paraphrase: The report will specify relevant threat models, including at least those already discussed.

context_stem: Factual information. A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Evidence (including evaluations) about relevant model capabilities and behaviors: For each in-scope model, capability and alignment evaluations (conducted internally and by external parties as appropriate), their results, and (as appropriate) other evidence we considered in assessing the level of risk.
paraphrase: For each in-scope model, the report will present capability/alignment evaluations, results, and other relevant risk evidence.

context_stem: Factual information. A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Risk mitigations: For each in-scope model, the mitigations we are implementing across security, deployment safeguards, and alignment domains, along with discussion of their effectiveness.
paraphrase: For each in-scope model, the mitigations across security, deployment, and alignment domains and their effectiveness will be documented.

context_stem: Factual information. A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Additional relevant factors: Any other considerations material to our risk analysis.
paraphrase: Other considerations material to the risk analysis will also be documented.

excerpt: Risk analyses. We will provide our reasoning and conclusions regarding both specific threat models and overall risk levels.
paraphrase: The report will provide reasoning and conclusions about both specific threat models and overall risk levels.

excerpt: Threat-specific risk assessment: For each threat model, we will analyze remaining absolute risk–i.e., the leftover risk after accounting for our mitigations.
paraphrase: For each threat model, the remaining absolute risk after mitigations will be analyzed.

excerpt: We will also discuss whether we believe we've crossed relevant thresholds in our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1), and (as relevant) whether we believe we're meeting the risk mitigation standards corresponding to them.
paraphrase: The report will discuss whether relevant industry-wide safety thresholds have been crossed and whether corresponding mitigation standards are being met.

excerpt: Overall risk assessment: We will provide an overall risk assessment.
paraphrase: An overall risk assessment will be provided.

excerpt: Risk-benefit determination: We will explain whether, and if so why, we believe the identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.
paraphrase: The report will explain whether identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.

excerpt: Looking forward: We will outline our plans for continuing to monitor and mitigate the relevant risks over time.
paraphrase: Plans to continue monitoring and mitigating risks over time will be outlined.

excerpt: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
paraphrase: The report will include a review of past Risk Reports and decisions.

context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Changes in risk mitigation practices—noteworthy cases in which our risk mitigation practices deviated (including temporarily) or changed from what we discussed in our previous Risk Report over the relevant period, and their implications for the overall level of risk.
paraphrase: Noteworthy deviations or changes in risk mitigation practices since the prior Risk Report, and their risk implications, will be addressed.

context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Decisions to internally deploy in-scope models that would not otherwise be reviewed in a Risk Report (because they happened in between Risk Reports).
paraphrase: The report will cover decisions to internally deploy in-scope models that occurred between Risk Reports and were not otherwise reviewed.

context_stem: Decisions to internally deploy in-scope models...
excerpt: We will discuss how these decisions were made and whether they appear reasonable in light of any noteworthy new information that has come to light since then.
paraphrase: The report will discuss how such deployment decisions were made and their reasonableness given new information.

context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Changes to our Frontier Safety Roadmap and any cases where we failed to meet our goals.
paraphrase: Changes to the Frontier Safety Roadmap and any missed goals will be addressed.

excerpt: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis. If we determine that the absolute level of risk being imposed industry-wide by AI systems such as ours is high, and are justifying our decision to move forward based partly on a marginal risk analysis, we will additionally address the following:
paraphrase: If industry-wide risk is judged high and marginal risk analysis partly justifies proceeding, additional topics will be addressed.

context_stem: we will additionally address the following:

paraphrase: The report will describe how model capabilities and mitigations compare to competitors.

context_stem: we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Role in risk assessment: How these comparisons factored into our risk assessment.
paraphrase: How competitor comparisons influenced the risk assessment will be described.

context_stem: we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Benefits analysis: The benefits, if any, of continuing to maintain our existing models or of advancing frontier capabilities, including considerations related to our mission and our ability to contribute to AI safety research and policy development.
paraphrase: Any benefits of maintaining existing models or advancing frontier capabilities, including mission-related considerations, will be analyzed.

context_stem: we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Advocacy efforts: The steps we took to raise public awareness of the relevant risks and to encourage appropriate regulatory action, including our engagement with policymakers and other AI developers.
paraphrase: Advocacy steps taken to raise awareness and encourage regulation, including policymaker and industry engagement, will be described.

excerpt: We will conduct the assessments above with respect to each in-scope model.
paraphrase: The described assessments will be conducted for each in-scope model.

excerpt: To avoid redundancy, we will likely analyze similar models collectively rather than individually, with appropriate justification for any such groupings.
paraphrase: Similar models may be analyzed together rather than individually, with justification, to reduce redundancy.

excerpt: Initial assessment and drafting: Our internal subject matter experts will conduct risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.
paraphrase: Internal subject matter experts will conduct risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.

excerpt: Review and feedback: We will solicit comprehensive internal feedback on the report, focusing on identifying potential methodological weaknesses, analytical gaps, or areas requiring additional evidence or clarification.
paraphrase: Comprehensive internal feedback will be sought to identify methodological weaknesses, gaps, or needed clarifications.

excerpt: We may also use this feedback to improve or refine the report itself.
paraphrase: Feedback may be used to refine the report.

excerpt: We will usually also seek feedback from trusted external parties with relevant expertise.
paraphrase: Feedback from trusted external experts will usually also be sought.

excerpt: Executive approval: The Risk Report, along with the internal feedback and any available external feedback, will be sent to the CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer (RSO) for final review and approval.
paraphrase: The Risk Report and feedback will be sent to the CEO and RSO for final review and approval.

excerpt: The CEO and RSO will make the ultimate determination regarding the adequacy of the risk assessment and any downstream deployment or development plans.
paraphrase: The CEO and RSO make the final determination on the adequacy of the risk assessment and related deployment or development plans.

excerpt: Governance notification: Following approval of a Risk Report, the CEO and RSO will promptly share their decision(s), the underlying Risk Report, and internal feedback with both the Board and the LTBT.
paraphrase: After approval, the CEO and RSO will promptly share the decision, Risk Report, and internal feedback with the Board and LTBT.

excerpt: Modified process when marginal risk analysis is important to our case. In the event that marginal risk analysis (see previous section) plays a major role in a decision to move forward, explicit approval of the Risk Report by the Board and LTBT (rather than just the CEO and RSO) will be required.
paraphrase: If marginal risk analysis plays a major role in a decision to proceed, explicit Board and LTBT approval is required instead of only CEO and RSO approval.

excerpt: By "marginal risk analysis," we mean arguing that the risks imposed by our systems in particular are relatively lower when keeping in mind the risks unavoidably posed by other AI systems.
paraphrase: The footnote defines marginal risk analysis as an argument comparing own-system risk to unavoidable risks posed by other AI systems.

excerpt: We will publish a public version of our Risk Report.
paraphrase: A public version of the Risk Report will be published.

excerpt: We will aim to minimize redactions to the public version of the report.
paraphrase: Redactions to the public version of the report will be minimized where possible.

excerpt: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
paraphrase: A non-exhaustive list of reasons for redaction follows.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Legal compliance: To comply with legal obligations on disclosing information, such as export control regulations, national security restrictions, or contractual obligations with third parties.
paraphrase: Redactions may be made to comply with legal obligations such as export controls, national security rules, or contracts.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Intellectual property protection: To protect proprietary information, including technical details of our models and training methodologies, trade secrets, or other confidential business information.
paraphrase: Redactions may protect proprietary information such as technical details, training methods, and trade secrets.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Public safety considerations: To protect public safety by not disclosing information that could be exploited to cause harm.
paraphrase: Redactions may protect public safety by withholding information that could be misused to cause harm.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Privacy: To protect the personal privacy of individuals.
paraphrase: Redactions may protect individuals' personal privacy.

excerpt: We will work toward a practice of seeking comprehensive, public external review on our Risk Reports.
paraphrase: Anthropic intends to work toward comprehensive, public external review of Risk Reports.

excerpt: This means working with one or more third-party organizations that will receive private versions of our Risk Reports (unredacted or with minimal redactions, as discussed below) and publish comprehensive commentary on them.
paraphrase: Third-party organizations will receive largely unredacted Risk Reports and publish comprehensive commentary.

excerpt: Commentary will address topics including the quality of our reasoning, the validity of our risk assessments, the overall level of risk, and whether the redactions we've made for the public version are reasonable and appropriate.
paraphrase: External commentary will cover reasoning quality, validity of assessments, overall risk level, and reasonableness of redactions.

excerpt: Our intent is for external reviewers' judgments to carry significant weight in the eyes of the public as well as our employees.
paraphrase: External reviewers' judgments are intended to carry significant weight with both the public and employees.

excerpt: But there are no well-established organizations or procedures for this sort of practice, and we are approaching it as an experiment.
paraphrase: Because no well-established organizations or procedures exist for this practice, it is being treated as an experiment.

excerpt: At a minimum, we will complete a full external review process (described below) with at least one external reviewer anytime a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted, defined as follows:
paraphrase: A full external review with at least one reviewer will be completed whenever a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted, as defined below.

excerpt: A model is "highly capable" if we conclude that it crosses the threshold for automated AI R&D described in Section 1.
paraphrase: A model is considered highly capable if it crosses the automated AI R&D threshold defined in Section 1.

excerpt: "Significantly redacted" means that the redactions omit information a reasonable external safety researcher would consider important in evaluating the overall level of risk, such that a reader of only the public version could not meaningfully assess whether they agree with our conclusions.
paraphrase: Significantly redacted means the omissions would prevent a reasonable external safety researcher from meaningfully assessing the risk conclusions from the public version alone.

excerpt: A report shall be deemed significantly redacted if, in the judgment of the RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT, it meets this description.
paraphrase: The RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT determine whether a report meets the significantly redacted definition.

excerpt: Note that unredacted reports will be shared with a large number of employees, who will be in a position to raise concerns if they believe the public version meets this description.
paraphrase: Unredacted reports are shared broadly with employees, who can raise concerns about the public version's redaction level.

excerpt: In consultation with the Board and LTBT, we will select external reviewers that:
paraphrase: External reviewers will be selected in consultation with the Board and LTBT, per the criteria below.

context_stem: we will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Have significant experience and expertise regarding evaluations for dangerous AI capabilities and propensities.
paraphrase: Reviewers must have significant expertise in evaluating dangerous AI capabilities and propensities.

excerpt: It's particularly important that they be knowledgeable about potential ways such evaluations might be misleading (for example, alignment faking).
paraphrase: Reviewers should be knowledgeable about ways evaluations could be misleading, such as alignment faking.

context_stem: we will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Have reputational and other incentives making them likely to be candid about their assessment of risks, rather than focused on writing comments that Anthropic will approve of.
paraphrase: Reviewers should have incentives favoring candor over pleasing Anthropic.

excerpt: For example, external review parties should not be teams whose revenue, reputation and success depend entirely on Anthropic and similar companies continuing to work with them.
paraphrase: External reviewers should not be entirely economically dependent on Anthropic and similar companies.

context_stem: we will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Do not have conflicts of interest with respect to Anthropic.
paraphrase: Reviewers must not have conflicts of interest regarding Anthropic.

context_stem: Do not have conflicts of interest with respect to Anthropic.
excerpt: At a minimum, a reviewing organization itself may not have a financial interest in Anthropic; and the individuals involved in conducting the review, as well as anyone above them in the reporting chain within their organization, may not have a financial interest in Anthropic or close personal relationships with anyone at Anthropic (i.e., family relationships, romantic relationships, or shared living arrangements).
paraphrase: Neither the reviewing organization nor the individuals conducting the review (nor their superiors) may hold a financial interest in Anthropic or close personal relationships with Anthropic staff.

excerpt: The external review process will involve sharing the Risk Report with one or more external reviewers within one week of submitting the same report to our Board and LTBT.
paraphrase: External reviewers will receive the Risk Report within one week of its submission to the Board and LTBT.

excerpt: We will ask the external reviewers to provide public commentary on our report within 30 days of receipt.
paraphrase: External reviewers will be asked to publish commentary within 30 days of receiving the report.

excerpt: We will try to work toward a process that involves the full external review being completed prior to Board/LTBT review (and may require this later).
paraphrase: Anthropic will attempt to complete full external review before Board/LTBT review, and may later make this mandatory.

excerpt: For purposes of external review, the only redactions to the Risk Report will be those necessary to comply with legal prohibitions or to maintain our legal rights.
paraphrase: Redactions for external review purposes are limited to those required for legal compliance or preserving legal rights.

excerpt: We expect that we will also invest some time in answering follow-up questions from parties doing external review.
paraphrase: Time is expected to be invested in answering follow-up questions from external reviewers.

excerpt: The external review will address:
paraphrase: The external review will cover the topics listed below.

excerpt: Adequacy of information: Whether the Risk Report contains sufficient information to assess the identified risks;
paraphrase: The review will assess whether the Risk Report contains sufficient information to evaluate identified risks.

excerpt: Analytical rigor: The strength of the Risk Report's reasoning and analysis;
paraphrase: The review will assess the strength of the report's reasoning and analysis.

excerpt: Areas of disagreement: Whether the external reviewer disagrees with any of the Risk Report's key claims and, if so, the reasons for any such disagreements; and
paraphrase: The review will note any disagreements with key claims and the reasons behind them.

excerpt: Risk reduction recommendations: Recommendations for further reducing identified risks.
paraphrase: The review will include recommendations for further reducing identified risks.

excerpt: The external reviewer will also evaluate our redaction decisions while avoiding disclosure of the redacted content itself.
paraphrase: The reviewer will also assess redaction decisions without disclosing the redacted material.

excerpt: In particular, the review will cover:
paraphrase: The review specifically covers the following redaction-related topics.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Redaction scope: The general nature and scope of redactions;
paraphrase: The review will describe the general nature and scope of redactions.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Redaction justification: Whether the external reviewer generally agrees or disagrees with the publicly stated reasons for the redactions and, if relevant, the reasons for any disagreements;
paraphrase: The review will state whether the reviewer agrees with the publicly stated redaction justifications and why, if disagreeing.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Balancing test: Whether the redactions strike a reasonable balance between Anthropic's legitimate interests and society's interest in transparency; and
paraphrase: The review will assess whether redactions reasonably balance Anthropic's interests against society's interest in transparency.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Materiality: Whether any of the redactions in the public report are material to any of the external reviewer's substantive disagreements with the report's claims.
paraphrase: The review will assess whether redactions materially affect the reviewer's substantive disagreements with the report.

excerpt: Public comments. We will ask the external reviewer to memorialize its findings on the topics above in a written report that is made public.
paraphrase: External reviewers will be asked to produce a public written report memorializing their findings.

excerpt: External reviewers will be bound by obligations not to disclose confidential information (e.g., confidential intellectual property, matters of national security, or proprietary details such as model architecture, cost, or size), but beyond that will not be restricted in what they can publish, including concerns about the Risk Report or Anthropic's conduct in connection with the external review.
paraphrase: Reviewers must keep confidential information private but otherwise face no restriction on publishing concerns, including about Anthropic's conduct.

excerpt: For example, we may redact information if sharing it would endanger our legal right to treat it as confidential. This would be an uncommon situation.
paraphrase: The footnote gives an example: redacting information to preserve a legal right to confidentiality, noted as uncommon.

excerpt: It does not mean we would redact information merely because it is sensitive or to reduce the risk of a leak.
paraphrase: Sensitivity alone or leak-risk reduction alone is not sufficient justification for redaction under this footnote.

excerpt: We commit to the following governance measures to promote internal and external accountability.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to governance measures for internal and external accountability.

excerpt: Responsible Scaling Officer: We will maintain the position of RSO, a designated member of staff who is responsible for the implementation of this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain an RSO position responsible for implementing the policy.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):

paraphrase: The RSO's duties include proposing policy updates, approving development/deployment decisions, and reviewing major contracts for policy consistency.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: (4) overseeing the implementation of this policy, including the allocation of sufficient resources; (5) receiving and addressing reports of potential instances of noncompliance; and (6) making judgment calls on policy interpretation and application.
paraphrase: The RSO's duties also include overseeing implementation and resource allocation, addressing noncompliance reports, and making interpretive judgment calls.

excerpt: Internal transparency: We will share final, unredacted Risk Reports with Anthropic's regular-clearance staff.
paraphrase: Anthropic will share complete, unredacted Risk Reports with regular-clearance staff.

excerpt: Noncompliance reporting: We will maintain a process for Anthropic staff to submit anonymous or identified reports regarding potential noncompliance with this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a process for staff to report noncompliance, anonymously or identified.

excerpt: Staff will have more than one option for who receives these reports, including the RSO, and at least one executive who does not report to the RSO.
paraphrase: Staff can choose among multiple report recipients, including the RSO and an executive independent of the RSO.

paraphrase: Upon receiving a report, Anthropic will investigate promptly, take proportional corrective action if substantiated, and document findings.

excerpt: We will provide quarterly updates to the Board regarding reports of potential noncompliance, whether substantiated or not.
paraphrase: Anthropic will give the Board quarterly updates on noncompliance reports regardless of substantiation.

excerpt: If we determine that a report is (1) substantiated and (2) involves a material safety risk, we will promptly notify the Board and we may provide public notice of the same.
paraphrase: If a report is substantiated and involves material safety risk, the Board is promptly notified and public notice may follow.

paraphrase: Anthropic will protect reporters from retaliation, and reports about the RSO must reach at least one Board member.

paraphrase: Anthropic will not use non-disparagement clauses that could discourage employees from raising safety concerns publicly.

paraphrase: Any non-disparagement clauses offered will not prevent raising safety concerns or disclosing the clause's existence.

paraphrase: Anthropic will regularly review its own implementation of the policy.

excerpt: Procedural compliance review: On approximately an annual basis, we will commission a third-party review that assesses whether we adhered to this policy's main procedural commitments.
paraphrase: Anthropic will commission an annual third-party review of procedural adherence to the policy.

excerpt: This review will focus on procedural compliance, not substantive outcomes.
paraphrase: The compliance review addresses procedure only, not substantive results.

paraphrase: RSP changes are proposed by the CEO and RSO and approved by the Board after consulting the LTBT.

excerpt: If we update the RSP, we will publicly share the updated version prior to or on its effective date and will record the differences from the prior draft in the Change Log.
paraphrase: Updated RSP versions are published by their effective date, with changes recorded in the Change Log.

excerpt: We will maintain the current version of the RSP on our website.
paraphrase: The current RSP version will be kept accessible on Anthropic's website.

locator: Table Appendix A / General upleveling / Commitment
excerpt: We will make a significant effort to meet or exceed that performance standard. However, we will not necessarily delay AI development and deployment in this scenario.
