excerpt: Earlier editions of our RSP defined "AI Safety Levels" with specific lists of required controls. We still use this concept to refer to, and distinguish between, present levels of risk mitigations—those that we maintain for existing AI models.
paraphrase: Prior RSP editions used ASLs with specific required controls; the concept still denotes present risk-mitigation levels for existing models.

excerpt: (For example, our initial Risk Report uses this distinction.)
paraphrase: An example is given: the initial Risk Report uses the present/future distinction.

excerpt: However, when defining the risk mitigations needed for future levels of AI capability, we have found that providing a specific list of controls is overly rigid, and we instead prefer to focus on what sort of argument an AI developer should make (and what sorts of actors it should address) regarding the risk level from its systems.
paraphrase: For future capability levels, Anthropic prefers argument-based reasoning over rigid control lists, focusing on the argument and relevant threat actors.

excerpt: RSP-2023 (aka RSP v1.0): Initial version.
paraphrase: The changelog entry for RSP v1.0 notes it as the initial version.

excerpt: RSP-2024: This update introduces a more flexible and nuanced approach to assessing and managing AI risks while maintaining our commitment not to train or deploy models unless we have implemented adequate safeguards.
paraphrase: The v2.0 update introduces a more flexible risk-management approach while retaining the commitment to adequate safeguards before training or deployment.

excerpt: Key improvements include new capability thresholds to indicate when we should upgrade our safeguards, refined processes for evaluating model capabilities and the adequacy of our safeguards (inspired by safety case methodologies), and new measures for internal governance and external input.
paraphrase: Key v2.0 improvements are new capability thresholds, refined evaluation processes inspired by safety cases, and new governance/external-input measures.

excerpt: We describe the most notable changes below.
paraphrase: The most notable changes are described in the following entries.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ASL definition changed
excerpt: ASL definition changed: The term "ASL" now refers to groups of technical and operational safeguards (it previously also referred to models). We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: The ASL term was redefined to refer only to safeguard groups rather than models, alongside new Capability Threshold and Required Safeguard concepts.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ASL definition changed
excerpt: This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
paraphrase: The redefinition enables safeguards to be targeted at specific capabilities rather than broad model categories.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: ARA threshold now a checkpoint: We replaced our previous autonomous replication and adaption (ARA) threshold with a "checkpoint" for autonomous AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The former ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint concept for autonomous AI capabilities.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: Rather than triggering higher safety standards automatically, reaching this checkpoint will prompt additional evaluation of the model's capabilities and accelerate our preparation of stronger safeguards.
paraphrase: Reaching the checkpoint triggers further evaluation and accelerated safeguard preparation, rather than automatic standard upgrades.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We previously considered these capabilities as a trigger for increased safeguards, motivated by an attempt to establish some threshold while we developed a better sense of potential threats.
paraphrase: These capabilities were formerly treated as a safeguard trigger while understanding of threats was still developing.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We now believe that these capabilities - at the levels we initially considered - would not necessitate the ASL-3 standard.
paraphrase: Anthropic now believes the originally considered capability levels do not require the ASL-3 standard.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / AI R&D threshold added
excerpt: AI R&D threshold added: We added a new threshold for AI systems that can significantly advance AI development.
paraphrase: A new threshold was added for AI systems that can significantly advance AI development.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / AI R&D threshold added
excerpt: Such capabilities could lead to rapid, unpredictable advances in AI, potentially outpacing our ability to evaluate and address emerging risks, and may also serve as an early warning sign for the ability to automate R&D in other domains.
paraphrase: These capabilities risk causing rapid unpredictable advances outpacing risk evaluation, and may indicate broader R&D automation ability.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
excerpt: Testing for Capability Thresholds: Rather than using prespecified evaluations, we now require an affirmative case that models are sufficiently far from Capability Thresholds.
paraphrase: Instead of prespecified evaluations, an affirmative case is now required showing sufficient distance from Capability Thresholds.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
excerpt: Predefined tests may miss emerging risks or be overly conservative relative to the actual threshold of concern.
paraphrase: Fixed tests risk missing new risks or being too conservative relative to the real threshold.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
excerpt: Our most accurate tests change frequently enough that it is more practical to use this new approach than to have our Board pre-approve evaluations.
paraphrase: Because tests change often, this new approach is more practical than Board pre-approval of evaluations.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Adjusted evaluation cadence
excerpt: Adjusted evaluation cadence: We adjusted the comprehensive assessment cadence to 4x Effective Compute or six months of accumulated post-training enhancements (this was previously three months).
paraphrase: The comprehensive assessment cadence was changed to 4x Effective Compute or six months of post-training enhancements, up from three months.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Adjusted evaluation cadence
excerpt: We found that a three-month cadence forced teams to prioritize conducting frequent evaluations over more comprehensive testing and improving methodologies.
paraphrase: The prior three-month cadence caused teams to favor frequency over comprehensiveness and methodological improvement.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: Less prescriptive evaluation methodology: We have replaced some specifics in our previous testing methodology (e.g., using 1% of compute for elicitation or creating a 6x buffer), with more general requirements to (a) match expected efforts of potential adversaries and (b) provide informal estimates of how further scaling and research developments will impact model capabilities and performance on the same tasks.
paraphrase: Specific prior methodology details like 1% compute for elicitation or a 6x buffer were replaced with general requirements to match adversary efforts and estimate future scaling impacts.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: We have found that specific methodologies may become outdated when new research developments are introduced.
paraphrase: Specific methodologies risk becoming outdated as new research emerges.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: Although still an aspirational goal, the science of evaluations is not currently mature enough to make confident predictions about the precise buffer we should require between current models and a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Precise buffer prediction remains aspirational because evaluation science is not yet mature enough for confident estimates.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: More outcome-focused safeguard requirements: We have updated our ASL-3 safeguards requirements to be less prescriptive and more outcome-focused.
paraphrase: ASL-3 safeguard requirements were made less prescriptive and more focused on outcomes.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: Rather than detailing specific operational and technical safeguards, we now specify the overall security or deployment standards and requirements for meeting them.
paraphrase: Instead of detailed specific safeguards, overall security/deployment standards and their requirements are now specified.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: This is to allow us to adapt our safeguards more flexibly as our understanding of risks and possible safeguards improves.
paraphrase: The change permits more flexible adaptation of safeguards as risk understanding improves.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models: We have clarified which actors are in and out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard.
paraphrase: The scope of actors relevant to the ASL-3 Security Standard was clarified.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
context_stem: Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models.
excerpt: We also removed the commitment to protect against scaled attacks and distillation attacks from the ASL-2 Security standard.
paraphrase: The ASL-2 Security standard no longer commits to protecting against scaled attacks and distillation attacks.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
context_stem: Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models.
excerpt: While distillation remains a concern for more capable models, models stored under ASL-2 safeguards have not yet reached potentially harmful Capability Thresholds.
paraphrase: Distillation is still a concern for more capable models, but ASL-2-safeguarded models have not reached harmful Capability Thresholds.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users: We have updated the ASL-3 Deployment Standard to allow for different levels of safeguards based on deployment context.
paraphrase: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard now permits differing safeguard levels depending on deployment context.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
context_stem: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users.
excerpt: For any general access systems, we still require passing intensive red-teaming.
paraphrase: General access systems still require passing intensive red-teaming.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
context_stem: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users.
excerpt: For internal use, safety testing and deployments to sufficiently trusted users, we will instead require a combination of access controls and monitoring.
paraphrase: For internal use, testing, and trusted-user deployments, a combination of access controls and monitoring is required instead.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
excerpt: New Capability and Safeguards Reports: We have introduced Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports.
paraphrase: Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports were introduced as new report types.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
excerpt: We expect that aggregating all the available evidence about model capabilities will provide decision makers with a more complete picture of the overall level of risk and improve our ability to solicit feedback on our work.
paraphrase: Aggregating capability evidence is expected to give decision-makers a fuller risk picture and improve feedback solicitation.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Internal and external accountability
excerpt: Internal and external accountability: We have made a number of changes to our previous "procedural commitments." These include expanding the duties of the Responsible Scaling Officer;
paraphrase: Several changes were made to procedural commitments, including expanding RSO duties.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Internal and external accountability
excerpt: adding internal critique and external expert input on capability and safeguard assessments; new procedures related to internal governance; and maintaining a public page for overviews of past Capability and Safeguard Reports, RSP-related updates, and future plans.
paraphrase: Additional changes added internal critique and external expert input, new internal governance procedures, and a public page for past reports and updates.

excerpt: RSP-2025: This update clarifies which Capability Thresholds would require enhanced safeguards beyond our current ASL-3 standards.
paraphrase: The v2.1 update clarifies which Capability Thresholds trigger safeguards beyond ASL-3.

excerpt: The key changes include:
paraphrase: A list of key changes follows.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.1 / New Capability Thresholds
excerpt: New Capability Thresholds: We have added a new capability threshold related to CBRN development, which defines capabilities that could substantially uplift the development capabilities of moderately resourced state programs.
paraphrase: A new CBRN-related capability threshold was added, defining capabilities that could substantially uplift moderately resourced state programs.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.1 / New Capability Thresholds
excerpt: We have also disaggregated our existing AI R&D capability thresholds, separating them into two distinct levels (the ability to fully automate entry-level AI research work, and the ability to cause dramatic acceleration in the rate of effective scaling) and provided additional detail on the corresponding Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: The AI R&D thresholds were split into two levels—automating entry-level research and dramatically accelerating effective scaling—with more detail on corresponding safeguards.

excerpt: Iterative Commitment: We have adopted a general commitment to reevaluate our Capability Thresholds whenever we upgrade to a new set of Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to reevaluating Capability Thresholds each time it upgrades Required Safeguards.

excerpt: We have decided not to maintain a commitment to define ASL-N+1 evaluations by the time we develop ASL-N models; such an approach would add unnecessary complexity because Capability Thresholds do not naturally come grouped in discrete levels.
paraphrase: Anthropic dropped the commitment to predefine next-level evaluations before reaching the current level, since thresholds do not naturally group discretely.

excerpt: We believe it is more practical and sensible instead to commit to reconsidering the whole list of Capability Thresholds whenever we upgrade our safeguards.
paraphrase: Reconsidering the entire list of Capability Thresholds at each safeguard upgrade is deemed more practical.

excerpt: ASL-3 Security: This update excludes both sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders from the ASL-3 Security Standard.
paraphrase: The v2.2 update excludes both sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders from the ASL-3 Security Standard.

excerpt: Previously, only "highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders" were explicitly excluded.
paraphrase: The prior exclusion covered only highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders.

excerpt: The model capabilities and threat models corresponding with the ASL-3 Security Standard do not warrant protection against either group: the CBRN-3 threat models entail large numbers of users having access to unguarded models (which is more likely to occur through a universal jailbreak than via model theft), and the relatively small number of employees who might be capable of model theft does not significantly affect the risk level.
paraphrase: Neither insider group needs protection under ASL-3, since CBRN-3 threats center on universal jailbreaks over model theft, and few employees could execute model theft anyway.

excerpt: For AI R&D-4, the threat models generally do not depend on model weight theft and instead entail AI systems engaging in autonomous internal sabotage.
paraphrase: For AI R&D-4, threat models center on autonomous internal sabotage rather than weight theft.

excerpt: This update is a comprehensive rewrite of our RSP. For a summary of changes and the thinking behind them, see here.
paraphrase: The v3.0 update is a full rewrite of the RSP, with a separate summary of changes referenced.

excerpt: This revision addresses the following points: (1) how we operationalize the Automated R&D capability threshold; (2) how we use internal feedback on Risk Reports; and (3) that we may consider pausing development or deployment even where the commitments described in Appendix A are not triggered.
paraphrase: The v3.1 revision covers operationalizing the Automated R&D threshold, using internal feedback on Risk Reports, and considering pauses even without Appendix A triggers.

excerpt: These changes are mostly clarificatory in nature; we don't see them as significant changes to substance.
paraphrase: The v3.1 changes are characterized as mostly clarificatory rather than substantive.

excerpt: Change (1) reflects further discussion of our operationalization of the capability threshold, and involves some substantive changes to make it better reflect our underlying intent.
paraphrase: Change (1) involves substantive changes to better reflect the intended meaning of the capability threshold.

excerpt: This update also includes minor edits for style or clarity.
paraphrase: The update also contains minor stylistic or clarity edits.
